title.zh: 卷二十八 列傳第十六: 陸俟 源賀 劉尼 薛提
title.en: Volume 28 Biographies 16: Lu Si, Yuan He, Liu Ni, Xue Ti
title.raw: 卷二十八 列傳第十六: 陸俟 源賀 劉尼 薛提 Volume 28 Biographies 16: Lu Si, Yuan He, Liu Ni, Xue Ti

sentences.zh: 陸俟 源賀 劉尼 薛提

translations.literal: Lu Si, Yuan He, Liu Ni, Xue Ti
translations.idiomatic: Lu Si, Yuan He, Liu Ni, and Xue Ti

sentences.zh: 陸俟源賀曾孫彪玄孫師師從叔雄劉尼薛提

translations.literal: Lu Si; Yuan He's great-grandson Biao, great-great-grandson Shi, Shi's uncle Xiong; Liu Ni; Xue Ti
translations.idiomatic: Lu Si; Yuan He — great-grandson Biao, great-great-grandson Shi, Shi's uncle Xiong; Liu Ni; Xue Ti

sentences.zh: 陸俟，代人也。

translations.literal: Lu Si was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Si was a native of Dai.

sentences.zh: 曾祖幹，祖引，世領部落。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Gan and grandfather Yin for generations led their tribal division.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Gan and grandfather Yin had led the tribe for generations.

sentences.zh: 父突，道武初帥部人從征伐，數有戰功，位離石鎮將、上党太守、關內侯。

translations.literal: His father Tu, at the beginning of Emperor Daowu's reign, led his tribesmen on campaigns and repeatedly won merit; he held the posts of Warden of Lishi, Administrator of Shangdang, and Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tu, in Daowu's early years, led the clansmen on campaign with repeated merit, rising to Warden of Lishi, Administrator of Shangdang, and Marquis Within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 俟少聰慧。

translations.literal: Si from youth was clever.
translations.idiomatic: Si was clever from boyhood.

sentences.zh: 明元踐祚，襲爵關內侯，位給事中，典選部、蘭台事，當官無所撓。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne, Si inherited the title Marquis Within the Passes, served as Supervising Attendant, oversaw the Selection Bureau and Orchid Terrace affairs, and in office bent to no pressure.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan acceded, Si inherited the marquisate, became Supervising Attendant, ran selection and the Orchid Terrace, and would not be swayed in office.

sentences.zh: 太武征赫連昌，詔俟督諸軍鎮以備蠕蠕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu attacked Helian Chang, he ordered Si to command the garrison forces against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu's campaign against Helian Chang sent Si to command frontier troops against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 與西平公安頡攻克武牢，賜爵建鄴公，拜冀州刺史。

translations.literal: With Prince of Xiping Anqi he stormed Wulao; he was enfeoffed Duke of Jianye and appointed Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince Anqi of Xiping he took Wulao, was made Duke of Jianye, and became Governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 時考州郡，唯俟與河內太守丘陳為天下第一。

translations.literal: At the time the court graded provinces and commanderies; only Si and Qiu Chen, Administrator of Henei, ranked first in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm was graded, only Si and Henei's Qiu Chen stood first.

sentences.zh: 轉武牢鎮大將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand General of the Wulao Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He became Grand General of the Wulao Garrison.

sentences.zh: 平涼休屠金崖、羌狄子玉等叛，復轉為安定鎮大將，追討崖等，皆獲之。

translations.literal: When the Xiutu of Pingliang, Jin Ya, Qiang Di Ziyu, and others rebelled, he was again made Grand General of the Anding Garrison, pursued Ya and the rest, and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: Pingliang's Xiutu Jin Ya, the Qiang Di Ziyu, and others rebelled; he was shifted to Anding, pursued them, and took them all.

sentences.zh: 遷懷荒鎮大將。

translations.literal: He was moved to Grand General of the Huaihuang Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Huaihuang as grand general.

sentences.zh: 未期，諸高車莫弗懼俟嚴急，請前鎮將郎孤。

translations.literal: Before his term ended, the Gao-che mo-fu chieftains, fearing Si's severity, asked for the former warden Lang Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Before his term ended, Gao-che mo-fu feared his harsh rule and asked for the former warden Lang Gu back.

sentences.zh: 太武許之。

translations.literal: Taiwu granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu agreed.

sentences.zh: 征俟，至京朝見，言不過周年，孤身必敗，高車必叛。

translations.literal: Si was recalled; at court he said that within a year Gu alone would fail and the Gao-che would rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he said Gu would fail within a year and the Gao-che would rise.

sentences.zh: 帝疑不實，切責之，以公歸第。

translations.literal: The emperor doubted the truth of it, rebuked him sharply, and sent him home with only his ducal title.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called it false, scolded him, and sent him home retaining only his rank.

sentences.zh: 明年，諸莫弗果殺孤以叛。

translations.literal: The next year the mo-fu indeed killed Gu and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Next year the mo-fu killed Gu and rebelled, as he had said.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之大驚，召俟問其故。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly startled and summoned Si to ask the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stunned and summoned Si to explain.

sentences.zh: 俟曰：「夫高車之俗，上下無禮，無禮之人，難為其上。

translations.literal: Si said: "The custom of the Gao-che sets no ritual between high and low; men without ritual are hard to rule from above.
translations.idiomatic: Si said, "Gao-che custom knows no ritual between high and low; the unruly are hard to govern.

sentences.zh: 臣蒞以威嚴，節之憲網，欲漸加訓導，使知分限。

translations.literal: Your servant governed with stern authority and bound them with law, wishing gradually to train and guide them so they would know their limits.
translations.idiomatic: I ruled with stern law, hoping to teach them their bounds.

sentences.zh: 而惡直醜正，實繁有徒，故訟臣無恩，稱孤之美。

translations.literal: But those who hate the upright and despise integrity are many; therefore they sued me as loveless and praised Gu's kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Many hate the upright; they called me harsh and praised Gu.

sentences.zh: 孤獲還鎮，欣其名譽，必加恩于百姓，譏臣為失，專欲以寬惠臨之，仁恕待之。

translations.literal: When Gu returned to command, delighted at his fame, he was sure to heap favor on the people, mock me as wrong, and aim to win them only by leniency and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Gu back in command would favor the people, mock my severity, and rule by indulgence alone.

sentences.zh: 無禮之人，易生陵傲，不過期年，無復上下。

translations.literal: Men without ritual easily grow insolent; within a year high and low would vanish.
translations.idiomatic: Without ritual, insolence spreads; within a year rank would collapse.

sentences.zh: 既無上下，然後收之以威，則人懷怨憝。

translations.literal: Once rank was gone, then to restrain them by force would fill men with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Then force would breed deep resentment.

sentences.zh: 怨憝既多，敗亂彰矣。

translations.literal: When resentment is many, defeat and disorder stand plain."
translations.idiomatic: Much resentment means open revolt."

sentences.zh: 」帝歎曰：「卿身乃短，慮何長也！

translations.literal: The emperor sighed: "Your body is short—how long your foresight!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed, "Short in stature, long in foresight!"

sentences.zh: 」即日復除散騎常侍。

translations.literal: That same day he was again appointed Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: That day he was reappointed Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝征蠕蠕，破涼州，常隨駕別督輜重。

translations.literal: On the emperor's Rouran campaign and the conquest of Liangzhou, he often followed the train and separately directed baggage trains.
translations.idiomatic: On the Rouran campaign and the fall of Liangzhou he followed the train and directed baggage.

sentences.zh: 又與高涼王那復渡河南略地。

translations.literal: Again with Prince of Gaoliang Na he crossed south of the Yellow River to raid territory.
translations.idiomatic: Again with Prince Na of Gaoliang he crossed the Yellow River to raid.

sentences.zh: 仍遷長安鎮大將。

translations.literal: He was then made Grand General of the Chang'an Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand General of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 與高涼王那擊蓋吳於杏城，獲吳二叔。

translations.literal: With Prince Na he struck Gai Wu at Xingcheng and captured Wu's two uncles.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince Na he fought Gai Wu at Xingcheng and took Wu's two uncles.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲送京師，俟獨不許，曰：「若不斬吳，恐長安之變未已。

translations.literal: The generals wished to send them to the capital; Si alone refused, saying: "If Wu is not beheaded, Chang'an's troubles may not end.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted them sent to the capital; Si refused: "Unless Wu dies, Chang'an may not rest.

sentences.zh: 一身藏竄，非其親信，誰能獲之？

translations.literal: One man in hiding—who but his intimates can seize him?
translations.idiomatic: One fugitive—only intimates can catch him.

sentences.zh: 若停十萬眾追一人，非上策也。

translations.literal: To halt a hundred thousand men to chase one man is not the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: Halting an army of a hundred thousand for one man is poor strategy.

sentences.zh: 不如私許吳叔，免其妻子，使自追吳。

translations.literal: Better secretly promise Wu's uncles freedom for their wives and children and let them hunt Wu themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Better promise the uncles their families and let them hunt Wu."

sentences.zh: 」諸將咸曰：「今獲其二叔，唯吳一人，何所復至？

translations.literal: The generals all said: "Now we have his two uncles; Wu is alone—what could he still do?"
translations.idiomatic: They said, "We hold both uncles; Wu is alone—what can he do?"

sentences.zh: 」俟曰：「諸君不見毒蛇乎？

translations.literal: Si said: "Have you never seen a venomous snake?
translations.idiomatic: Si said, "Have you never seen a viper?"

sentences.zh: 不斷其頭，猶能為害。

translations.literal: If you do not cut off its head, it can still harm.
translations.idiomatic: Uncut, its head still kills.

sentences.zh: 況除腹心之疾，而曰必遺其類，可乎？

translations.literal: How, when removing a disease of the heart, can you say its kind must be left—can that be right?"
translations.idiomatic: When excising a heart's disease, who leaves the brood?"

sentences.zh: 」遂舍吳二叔，與之期。

translations.literal: He therefore released Wu's two uncles and set a deadline with them.
translations.idiomatic: He released the uncles and set a date.

sentences.zh: 及期，吳叔不至，諸將皆咎俟。

translations.literal: When the day came the uncles did not appear; the generals all blamed Si.
translations.idiomatic: The day passed without them; all blamed Si.

sentences.zh: 俟曰：「此未得其便耳，必不背也。

translations.literal: Si said: "They have not yet found their chance; they will not break faith."
translations.idiomatic: Si said, "They lack opportunity; they will not betray us."

sentences.zh: 」後數日，果斬吳以至，皆如其言。

translations.literal: Days later Wu was indeed beheaded and brought in—everything as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Wu's head arrived—exactly as he foretold.

sentences.zh: 俟之明略獨決，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Si's clear strategy and solitary decisions were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Si's foresight and solitary resolve were always thus.

sentences.zh: 遷內都大官。

translations.literal: He was moved to Grand Director of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: He became Grand Director of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 安定盧水劉超等叛，太武以俟威恩被關中，詔以本官加都督秦、雍諸軍，鎮長安。

translations.literal: When Liu Chao and others of Anding's Lushui rebelled, Taiwu, because Si's authority and kindness extended through Guanzhong, ordered him in his existing office additionally to be Area Commander of Qin and Yong forces, garrisoning Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chao of Lushui rebelled in Anding; Taiwu, knowing Si's name in Guanzhong, made him Area Commander of Qin and Yong while keeping his post at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「超等恃險，不順王命，朕若以重兵與卿，則超等必合為一；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Chao and the rest rely on terrain and disobey the royal command. If I give you a heavy force, Chao will surely unite with them;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Chao holds the passes; a heavy force unites them;

sentences.zh: 若以輕兵與卿，則不制矣。

translations.literal: if I give you a light force, you cannot control them.
translations.idiomatic: a light force cannot hold them.

sentences.zh: 今使卿以方略定之。

translations.literal: Now I send you to settle them by strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Go settle them by stratagem."

sentences.zh: 」於是俟單馬之鎮。

translations.literal: Si therefore rode alone to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Si rode alone to command.

sentences.zh: 既至，申揚威信，示以成敗，超猶無降意。

translations.literal: On arrival he proclaimed authority and showed success and failure; Chao still had no mind to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed majesty and showed outcomes; Chao would not yield.

sentences.zh: 俟乃率其帳下見超。

translations.literal: Si then led his personal guard to see Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Si led his guard to call on Chao.

sentences.zh: 超使人逆曰：「三百人以外，當以弓馬相待；

translations.literal: Chao sent word ahead: "Beyond three hundred men, bow and horse are the greeting;
translations.idiomatic: Chao warned, "Past three hundred, expect bows;

sentences.zh: 三百人以內，當以酒食相供。

translations.literal: within three hundred, wine and food will be provided."
translations.idiomatic: within three hundred, wine and meat."

sentences.zh: 」乃將二百騎詣超。

translations.literal: He therefore took two hundred horsemen to Chao.
translations.idiomatic: He took two hundred riders to Chao.

sentences.zh: 超備甚嚴，遂縱酒，盡醉而還。

translations.literal: Chao's guard was very strict; they drank until all were drunk and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's guard was tight; they drank to drunkenness and left.

sentences.zh: 後偽獵，詣超。

translations.literal: Later, feigning a hunt, he went to Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Later he feigned a hunt and visited Chao.

sentences.zh: 與士卒約曰：「今會發機，當以醉為限。

translations.literal: He agreed with his soldiers: "When we strike today, drunkenness is the signal."
translations.idiomatic: He told his men, "When we move, feign drunkenness."

sentences.zh: 」俟乃詐醉，上馬大呼，斬超首。

translations.literal: Si then pretended drunkenness, mounted, shouted, and beheaded Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Si played drunk, mounted, shouted, and struck off Chao's head.

sentences.zh: 士卒應聲縱擊，遂平之。

translations.literal: The soldiers answered with a shout and charged; the rebellion was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: His men charged at once; the rebellion ended.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，徵拜外都大官。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and summoned him as Grand Director of the Outer Court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejoiced and made him Grand Director of the Outer Court.

sentences.zh: 文成踐祚，以子麗有定策勳，進爵東平王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng took the throne, because his son Li had merit in settling the succession, Si was advanced to Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng's accession, with son Li's merit in the succession, raised Si to Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 薨，年六十七，諡成王。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-seven; posthumous name Prince Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-seven, posthumous name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 有子十二人。

translations.literal: He had twelve sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had twelve sons.

sentences.zh: 長子珝，多智，有父風。

translations.literal: The eldest, Xu, was very clever and had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Xu was clever and like his father.

sentences.zh: 文成見而悅之，謂朝臣曰：「吾常歎其父智過其軀，是復逾于父矣！

translations.literal: Wencheng saw him and was pleased, telling the court: "I often sighed that his father's wisdom exceeded his frame—this one surpasses his father!"
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng met him and said, "His father's mind outgrew his body—this boy outgrows his father!"

sentences.zh: 」少為內都下大夫。

translations.literal: In youth he was Junior Grand Master of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served as Junior Grand Master of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 奉上接下，行止取與，每能逆曉人意。

translations.literal: Serving superiors and receiving subordinates, in conduct and gift he could always anticipate others' wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Up and down the ranks he anticipated every wish in bearing and gift.

sentences.zh: 與其從事者無不愛之。

translations.literal: None who worked with him failed to love him.
translations.idiomatic: All who served with him loved him.

sentences.zh: 興安初，賜爵聊城侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xing'an he was enfeoffed Marquis of Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: At Xing'an's start he was made Marquis of Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 出為相州刺史，假長廣公。

translations.literal: Sent out as Governor of Xiang Province, with acting title Prince of Changguang.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Governor of Xiang, acting Prince of Changguang.

sentences.zh: 為政清平，抑強扶弱。

translations.literal: His government was clear and level; he curbed the strong and aided the weak.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled plainly, curbing the strong and helping the weak.

sentences.zh: 州中有德宿老名望素重者，以友禮待之。

translations.literal: In the province were venerable elders of long-standing virtue and fame; he treated them with the rites due friends.
translations.idiomatic: He honored aged men of local renown as friends.

sentences.zh: 詢之政事，責以方略，如此者十人，號曰十善。

translations.literal: He questioned them on administration and charged them with strategy; there were ten such men, called the Ten Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Ten such elders he called the Ten Worthies and charged with counsel.

sentences.zh: 又簡取諸縣強門百餘人以為假子。

translations.literal: He also selected more than a hundred strong-house sons from the counties as his foster sons.
translations.idiomatic: He took over a hundred strong-house sons as foster sons.

sentences.zh: 誘接殷勤，賜以衣服，令各歸家為耳目。

translations.literal: He received them warmly, gave them clothes, and sent each home as his eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: He clothed them and sent them home as informants.

sentences.zh: 於是發奸擿伏，事無不驗。

translations.literal: Thus hidden wrongdoing was exposed; nothing failed to prove true.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden crime surfaced; nothing failed to check.

sentences.zh: 百姓以為神明，無敢劫盜者。

translations.literal: The people thought him divine; none dared rob or steal.
translations.idiomatic: The people called him divine; robbery ceased.

sentences.zh: 在州七年，家至貧約。

translations.literal: Seven years in the province, his household remained utterly poor.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years in office, his house stayed poor.

sentences.zh: 徵為散騎常侍，百姓乞留珝者千餘人。

translations.literal: Summoned as Regular Attendant, more than a thousand people begged to keep Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Regular Attendant, over a thousand petitioned to keep him.

sentences.zh: 獻文不許，謂群臣曰：「珝之善政，雖古人何以加之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen would not agree and told the ministers: "Xu's good government—what ancient could add to it?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianwen refused and told the court, "What ancient surpassed Xu's rule?"

sentences.zh: 」賜絹五百匹，奴婢十口。

translations.literal: He granted five hundred bolts of silk and ten slaves and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: He gave five hundred bolts of silk and ten slaves.

sentences.zh: 珝之代還也，吏人大斂布帛以遺之。

translations.literal: When Xu left office, clerks and people heaped cloth and silk to give him.
translations.idiomatic: On his departure clerks and people piled gifts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 珝皆不受，人亦不取，於是以此物起佛寺焉，因名長廣公寺。

translations.literal: Xu accepted none; the people would not take their gifts back either, and with that cloth they raised a Buddhist temple, hence named the Temple of Prince Changguang.
translations.idiomatic: He refused all; the people built a temple from the cloth, the Temple of Prince Changguang.

sentences.zh: 後襲父爵，改封建安王。

translations.literal: Later he inherited his father's title and was changed to Prince of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He later inherited and was made Prince of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 琇字伯琳，珝第五子也。

translations.literal: Xiu, styled Bolin, was Xu's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu, styled Bolin, was Xu's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 母赫連氏身長七尺九寸，甚有婦德。

translations.literal: His mother, of the Helian clan, stood seven chi nine cun tall and had great wifely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Helian stood seven chi nine cun and was deeply virtuous.

sentences.zh: 珝有以爵傳琇之意。

translations.literal: Xu intended to pass the title to Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu meant the title for Xiu.

sentences.zh: 琇年九歲，珝謂之曰：「汝祖東平王有十二子，我為嫡長，承襲家業。

translations.literal: When Xiu was nine, Xu told him: "Your grandfather the Prince of Dongping had twelve sons; I am the eldest legitimate son and inherited the house.
translations.idiomatic: At nine Xiu heard, "Your grandfather had twelve sons; I am eldest and heir.

sentences.zh: 今已年老，屬汝幼沖，詎堪為陸氏宗首乎？

translations.literal: Now I am old and leave you still young—can you bear to be head of the Lu clan?"
translations.idiomatic: I am old and you a child—can you head the house?"

sentences.zh: 」琇對曰：「苟非鬥力，何患童幼！

translations.literal: Xiu answered: "If it is not a contest of strength, why fear being young!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiu said, "If it is not wrestling, why fear youth?"

sentences.zh: 」珝奇之，遂立琇為世子。

translations.literal: Xu marveled and made Xiu his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Xu marveled and named him heir.

sentences.zh: 珝薨，襲爵。

translations.literal: When Xu died, Xiu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu inherited on Xu's death.

sentences.zh: 琇沈毅少言，雅好讀書。

translations.literal: Xiu was deep, steady, and sparing of words; he loved reading.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was grave, quiet, and fond of books.

sentences.zh: 以功臣子孫，為侍御長，累遷祠部尚書、司州大中正。

translations.literal: As a meritorious minister's descendant he was Chief of the Imperial Guard, then rose to Minister of the Imperial Clan and Grand Rectifier of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: A minister's son, he became Chief of the Imperial Guard, then Minister of the Imperial Clan and Grand Rectifier of Si.

sentences.zh: 會從兄睿事，免官。

translations.literal: When his cousin Rui's affair broke out, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Rui's scandal cost him his post.

sentences.zh: 景明初，試守河內郡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming he was tried as Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming he tried governing Henei.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧謀反，令子曇和等先據河內。

translations.literal: Prince of Xianyang Xi rebelled and sent his son Tanhe and others first to seize Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi of Xianyang rebelled and sent son Tanhe to seize Henei.

sentences.zh: 琇聞禧反，斬曇和首。

translations.literal: Hearing of Xi's revolt, Xiu beheaded Tanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the revolt, Xiu beheaded Tanhe.

sentences.zh: 時以琇不先送曇和，禧敗始斬，責其通情，徵詣廷尉。

translations.literal: At the time, because Xiu had not sent Tanhe ahead and only beheaded him after Xi's defeat, he was charged with collusion and summoned to the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had not sent Tanhe up earlier and only killed him after Xi's fall, he was charged with collusion and haled to the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 少卿崔振窮罪狀，案琇大逆。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Cui Zhen exhausted the evidence and judged Xiu guilty of great treason.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Cui Zhen built the case and condemned him for treason.

sentences.zh: 陸宗大小，咸見收捕。

translations.literal: The Lu clan great and small were all seized.
translations.idiomatic: Great and small of the Lu house were arrested.

sentences.zh: 會將赦，先斃於獄。

translations.literal: When an amnesty was due, he was first executed in prison.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty was coming; he was killed in prison first.

sentences.zh: 琇弟凱仍上書訴冤，宣武詔復琇爵，子景詐襲。

translations.literal: Xiu's younger brother Kai still memorialized for justice; Emperor Xuanwu ordered Xiu's title restored and his son Jing to inherit falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Kai petitioned; Xuanwu restored Xiu's rank and let son Jing inherit.

sentences.zh: 凱字智君，謹重好學。

translations.literal: Kai, styled Zhijun, was careful, weighty, and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Kai, styled Zhijun, was careful and scholarly.

sentences.zh: 位太子庶子、給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was Junior Tutor and Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 凱在樞要十餘年，以忠厚見稱。

translations.literal: Kai spent more than ten years at the pivot and was praised for loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years at court won him praise for loyalty.

sentences.zh: 後遇患，頻上書乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Later, when ill, he repeatedly memorialized begging to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Illness drove him to beg retirement again and again.

sentences.zh: 除正平太守，在郡七年，號為良吏。

translations.literal: Made Administrator of Zhengping; seven years in the commandery, he was called a good official.
translations.idiomatic: Made Administrator of Zhengping; seven years there made him a model magistrate.

sentences.zh: 初，孝文將議革變舊風，大臣並有難色。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Xiaowen was about to discuss reforming old customs, the great ministers all looked troubled.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowen planned to reform old ways, ministers looked troubled.

sentences.zh: 又每引劉芳、郭祚等，常與規謀，共論政事。

translations.literal: He also often summoned Liu Fang, Guo Zuo, and others to plan with them and discuss government.
translations.idiomatic: He often summoned Liu Fang, Guo Zuo, and others to plot policy.

sentences.zh: 而國戚謂遂疏己，怏怏有不平之色。

translations.literal: The imperial kin thought themselves now slighted and nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kin felt slighted and grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 帝乃令凱私喻之曰：「至尊但欲廣知前事，直當問其古式耳。

translations.literal: The emperor had Kai secretly explain to them: "His Majesty only wishes to broaden knowledge of former affairs and will simply ask about ancient forms.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Kai tell them, "The throne only seeks to learn the old forms.

sentences.zh: 終無寵彼而疏國戚舊人意。

translations.literal: He will never favor them and slight the old imperial kin."
translations.idiomatic: He will not favor newcomers over kin."

sentences.zh: 」乃稍解。

translations.literal: They then gradually relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: Resentment eased.

sentences.zh: 及兄琇陷罪，凱亦被收，遇赦乃免。

translations.literal: When brother Xiu fell into crime, Kai was also seized but escaped through amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu fell, Kai was seized but amnestied.

sentences.zh: 凱痛兄之死，哭無時節，目幾失明，訴冤不已。

translations.literal: Kai grieved his brother's death, wept without regard to season, nearly went blind, and pleaded injustice without end.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned Xiu without cease, nearly blind, pleading injustice.

sentences.zh: 至正始初，宣武復琇官爵。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Zhengshi, Xuanwu restored Xiu's office and title.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhengshi's start Xuanwu restored Xiu's honors.

sentences.zh: 凱大喜，置酒集諸親曰：「吾所以數年之中抱病忍死者，顧門計耳，今願已遂。

translations.literal: Kai rejoiced greatly, set out wine, and gathered kin, saying: "These many years I bore illness and endured death for the clan's sake alone; now my wish is fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: Kai feasted his kin: "Years I clung to life for the house—now it is done."

sentences.zh: 」以其年卒，贈龍驤將軍、南青州刺史，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: In that year he died; posthumously made General of Dragon Cavalry and Governor of Southern Qing, posthumous name Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He died that year, posthumously Dragon Cavalry General and Governor of Southern Qing, posthumous name Hui.

sentences.zh: 長子痈，字道暉，與弟恭之並有時譽。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yong, styled Daohui, and his brother Gongzhi both had contemporary fame.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest Yong, styled Daohui, and brother Gongzhi were famed.

sentences.zh: 洛陽令賈禎見其兄弟，歎曰：「僕以老年，更睹雙璧。

translations.literal: Luoyang Magistrate Jia Zhen saw the brothers and sighed: "I thought my old age done—yet I see a pair of jades again."
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Jia Zhen sighed, "I thought my age over—yet two jades shine again."

sentences.zh: 」又嘗兄弟共候黃門郎孫惠蔚。

translations.literal: Once the brothers together waited on Yellow Gate Attendant Sun Huiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Once they waited together on Sun Huiwei of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 謂諸賓曰：「不意二陸，復在坐隅。

translations.literal: He told the guests: "I did not expect the two Lus still in the corner.
translations.idiomatic: He told guests, "The two Lus still grace the corner.

sentences.zh: 吾德謝張公，無以延譽。

translations.literal: My virtue falls short of Lord Zhang—I have no praise to offer."
translations.idiomatic: I lack Zhang's grace to praise them."

sentences.zh: 」痈位尚書右戶、三公郎，坐事免。

translations.literal: Yong held the posts of Right Master of the Household in the Ministry of Revenue and Gentleman of the Three Offices; dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was Master of Revenue and Gentleman of the Three Offices, then dismissed.

sentences.zh: 後除伏波將軍。

translations.literal: Later made General Who Subdues Waves.
translations.idiomatic: Later General Who Subdues Waves.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈冠軍、恆州刺史。

translations.literal: At death posthumously Champion General and Governor of Heng.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Champion General and Governor of Heng.

sentences.zh: 痈擬《急就篇》為《悟蒙章》，及《七誘》、《十醉》，章表數十篇。

translations.literal: Yong modeled the Jijiu Pian as Wumeng Zhang, and Seven Enticements and Ten Drunkennesses—several dozen chapters of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Yong wrote Wumeng Zhang after Jijiu, plus Seven Enticements, Ten Drunkennesses, and dozens of memorials.

sentences.zh: 痈與恭之晚不和睦，為時所鄙。

translations.literal: Yong and Gongzhi in later years were not harmonious and were scorned by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life Yong and Gongzhi quarreled and were scorned.

sentences.zh: 子元規位尚書郎。

translations.literal: His son Yuan Gui held the post of Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yuan Gui was a Masters of Writing gentleman.

sentences.zh: 元規子撥，陰陽律曆，多所通解，位并州長流參軍。

translations.literal: Yuan Gui's son Bo, versed in yin-yang and calendrics, held the post of Senior Clerk of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bo mastered yin-yang and calendars and was Senior Clerk of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 恭之字季順，有操尚，位東荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Gongzhi, styled Jishun, had integrity and held the post of Governor of Eastern Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhi, styled Jishun, was upright and Governor of Eastern Jing.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: Posthumously Minister of the Civil Service, posthumous name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Minister of Civil Service, posthumous name Yi.

sentences.zh: 恭之所著文章詩賦凡千餘篇。

translations.literal: Gongzhi's writings, poems, and fu totaled more than a thousand pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His writings exceeded a thousand pieces.

sentences.zh: 子曄，字仁崇，篤志文學，《齊律》序則仁崇之詞。

translations.literal: His son Ye, styled Renchong, devoted to letters; the preface to the Qi Code is Renchong's wording.
translations.idiomatic: Son Ye, styled Renchong, wrote the preface to the Qi Code.

sentences.zh: 位終通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He ended as Regular Attendant Direct and Unimpeded.
translations.idiomatic: His last post was Regular Attendant Direct and Unimpeded.

sentences.zh: 弟寬，字仁惠，太子中舍人，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: His younger brother Kuan, styled Renhui, was Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and attendant at the Forest of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: Younger Kuan, styled Renhui, was Junior Mentor and Forest of Literature attendant.

sentences.zh: 寬兄弟並有才品，議者稱為三武。

translations.literal: The Kuan brothers all had talent; critics called them the Three Martial.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were called the Three Martial.

sentences.zh: 珝弟歸，位東宮舍人、駕部校尉。

translations.literal: Xu's younger brother Gui held the posts of Eastern Palace Attendant and Commandant of the Imperial Transport.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Gui was Eastern Palace Attendant and Transport Commandant.

sentences.zh: 子珍，夏州刺史，贈太僕卿，諡曰靜。

translations.literal: His son Zhen was Governor of Xia Province, posthumously Grand Master of the Imperial Stud, posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhen governed Xia, posthumously Grand Master of the Stud, posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 珍子旭，性雅淡，好《易》、緯候之學，撰《五星要決》及《兩儀真圖》，頗得其指要。

translations.literal: Zhen's son Xu was refined and quiet, fond of the Changes and apocryphal astrology; he compiled Essentials of the Five Stars and the True Chart of the Two Poles and grasped their essentials well.
translations.idiomatic: Xu loved the Changes and omen lore, wrote on the Five Stars and the Two Poles, and mastered their core.

sentences.zh: 太和中，徵拜中書博士，稍遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was summoned as Erudite of the Secretariat and gradually promoted to Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe he became Secretariat erudite, then Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 知天下將亂，遂隱於太行山，屢征不起。

translations.literal: Seeing the realm would fall into disorder, he hid on Mount Taihang and repeatedly refused summons.
translations.idiomatic: Foreseeing chaos, he hid on Taihang and refused summons.

sentences.zh: 卒後，贈並、汾、恆、肆四州刺史。

translations.literal: After death he was posthumously made Governor of Bing, Fen, Heng, and Si.
translations.idiomatic: After death he was posthumously governor of four provinces.

sentences.zh: 子騰。

translations.literal: His son Teng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Teng.

sentences.zh: 騰字顯聖，少慷慨有大節。

translations.literal: Teng, styled Xiansheng, from youth was bold and had great integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Teng, styled Xiansheng, was bold and high-minded from youth.

sentences.zh: 從爾硃榮平葛榮，以功賜爵清河縣伯。

translations.literal: Following Erzhu Rong he pacified Ge Rong and for merit was enfeoffed Baron of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: With Erzhu Rong he crushed Ge Rong and was made Baron of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 稍遷通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Regular Attendant Direct and Unimpeded.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Regular Attendant Direct and Unimpeded.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，時使青州，遂留鄴，為陽城郡守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, he was on mission in Qingzhou and stayed at Ye as Administrator of Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu fled west, Teng was in Qingzhou and stayed at Ye as Yangcheng magistrate.

sentences.zh: 大統九年，大軍東討陽城，被執。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Datong the eastern army attacked Yangcheng and took him.
translations.idiomatic: Datong 9 the eastern army took Yangcheng and captured him.

sentences.zh: 周文帝釋而與語，騰盛論東州人物，又敘述時事，辭理抑揚。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou released him and spoke with him; Teng discoursed at length on Eastern Province worthies and reviewed current affairs with rising and falling eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's Emperor Wen freed him; Teng praised eastern men and debated affairs with eloquence.

sentences.zh: 周文歎曰：「卿真不背本也！

translations.literal: Wen sighed: "You truly do not betray your roots!"
translations.idiomatic: Wen sighed, "You have not betrayed your roots!"

sentences.zh: 」即拜帳內大都督。

translations.literal: He was at once made Grand Commander within the Tent.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Commander within the Tent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除太子庶子，遷武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Before long, Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, then Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Junior Tutor, then Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 騰既為周文所知，國欲立功，不願內職。

translations.literal: Once known to Wen, Teng wished to win merit abroad and did not want inner posts.
translations.idiomatic: Known to Wen, he wanted frontier merit, not palace posts.

sentences.zh: 及安康賊黃眾寶等作亂，攻圍東梁州。

translations.literal: When the Ankang bandit Huang Zhongbao and others rebelled and besieged Eastern Liangzhou,
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Zhongbao besieged Eastern Liangzhou,

sentences.zh: 城中糧盡，詔騰率軍大破之。

translations.literal: provisions in the city were exhausted; an edict ordered Teng to lead troops and smash them.
translations.idiomatic: stores ran out; Teng was sent and broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 軍還，拜龍州刺史。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was made Governor of Long.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was Governor of Long.

sentences.zh: 使通江油路，直出南秦。

translations.literal: He was sent to open the Tongjiang route straight to Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the Tongjiang road to Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 周文謂曰：「此是卿取柱國之日。

translations.literal: Wen told him: "This is the day you earn your pillar rank."
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, "Today you earn pillar rank."

sentences.zh: 」即解所服金帶賜之。

translations.literal: He at once removed his own gold belt and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Teng his own gold belt.

sentences.zh: 州人李廣嗣、李武等憑據岩險，曆政不能制。

translations.literal: The provincials Li Guangsi and Li Wu held rugged passes; successive administrations could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangsi and Li Wu held the mountains; no governor broke them.

sentences.zh: 騰密令多造飛梯，夜襲破之，執廣嗣等於鼓下。

translations.literal: Teng secretly had many scaling ladders made and by night stormed and broke them, seizing Guangsi and the rest below the drum.
translations.idiomatic: Teng built ladders, struck by night, and seized them at the drum.

sentences.zh: 其党有任公忻，圍逼州城，請免廣嗣及武，即散兵請罪。

translations.literal: Their party had Ren Gongxin, who besieged the prefectural city and asked that Guangsi and Wu be spared to disperse the troops and beg pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Gongxin besieged the city and begged mercy for Guangsi and Wu.

sentences.zh: 騰謂將士曰：「吾不殺廣嗣等，可謂墮軍實而長寇仇。

translations.literal: Teng told the soldiers: "If I do not kill Guangsi and the rest, I may be said to waste the army's gain and grow the foe."
translations.idiomatic: Teng said, "Spare them and I waste victory and feed the enemy."

sentences.zh: 」即斬廣嗣及武，以首示之。

translations.literal: He then beheaded Guangsi and Wu and displayed the heads.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded both and showed the heads.

sentences.zh: 於是出兵奮擊，盡獲之。

translations.literal: He then led troops in fierce attack and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: Then he charged and took all.

sentences.zh: 進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，轉江州刺史，進爵上庸縣公。

translations.literal: Promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, Commissioner with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, transferred to Governor of Jiang, advanced to Duke of Shangyong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Agile Cavalry General and Commissioner, became Governor of Jiang, Duke of Shangyong.

sentences.zh: 陵州木籠獠恃險，每行抄劫，詔騰討之。

translations.literal: The Mulong Liao of Lingzhou relied on terrain; they constantly raided.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhou's Mulong Liao raided from the hills.

sentences.zh: 獠因山為城，攻之未可拔。

translations.literal: The Liao made mountains their walls; assault could not take them.
translations.idiomatic: They walled the mountains; assault failed.

sentences.zh: 騰遂於城下多設聲樂及諸雜伎，示無戰心。

translations.literal: Teng then set up much music and miscellaneous entertainments below the walls to show no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: He staged music and shows below the walls, feigning peace.

sentences.zh: 諸賊果棄其兵仗，或攜妻子臨城觀樂。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed cast aside arms; some brought wives and children to watch from the walls.
translations.idiomatic: They dropped weapons and brought families to watch.

sentences.zh: 騰知其無備，遂縱兵討擊，盡殺破之。

translations.literal: Teng knew them unprepared and loosed troops to strike; all were killed or broken.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing them slack, he attacked and destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 周明帝初，陵、眉等八州夷夏並反，攻破郡縣，騰率兵討平之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming of Zhou, the Yi and Xia of eight provinces of Ling and Mei all rebelled and stormed commanderies and counties; Teng led troops and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Ming of Zhou's start saw eight provinces rebel; Teng pacified them.

sentences.zh: 及齊公憲作鎮於蜀，以騰為隆州刺史，令憲入蜀兵馬鎮防，皆委騰統攝。

translations.literal: When Duke of Qi Xian was stationed in Shu, Teng was made Governor of Long and all troops Xian brought into Shu for defense were entrusted to Teng's command.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xian of Qi in Shu made Teng Governor of Long and gave him all garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 赴公招代憲，復請留之。

translations.literal: Duke Zhao came to replace Xian and again asked to keep Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao replaced Xian and kept Teng.

sentences.zh: 遷隆州總管，領刺史。

translations.literal: Moved to Area Commander of Long, concurrently Governor.
translations.idiomatic: He became Area Commander of Long, still governor.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，資州石槃人反，殺郡守，據險自守，州軍不能制。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, the Shiban people of Zizhou rebelled, killed the commandery administrator, held the passes, and provincial troops could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Baoding 2, Zizhou's Shiban rebels killed the magistrate and held the hills.

sentences.zh: 騰率軍討擊，盡破斬之。

translations.literal: Teng led troops to strike and broke and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: Teng crushed and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 而蠻子反，所在蜂起，山路險阻，難得掩襲。

translations.literal: Then southern barbarians rebelled everywhere along the mountain roads, hard to surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Then hill barbarians rose on every road.

sentences.zh: 遂量山川形勢，隨便開道。

translations.literal: He therefore measured terrain and opened roads as needed.
translations.idiomatic: He surveyed terrain and cut roads where needed.

sentences.zh: 蠻獠畏威，承風請服。

translations.literal: The Liao feared his might and came to submit on the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians submitted to his awe.

sentences.zh: 所開之路，多得古銘，並是諸葛亮、桓溫舊道。

translations.literal: Roads he opened often bore ancient inscriptions—old tracks of Zhuge Liang and Huan Wen.
translations.idiomatic: His roads uncovered inscriptions—tracks of Zhuge Liang and Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 是年，鐵山獠抄斷內江路，使驛不通。

translations.literal: That year, Tieshan Liao cut the inner Jiang route so couriers could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: That year Tieshan Liao cut the inner river courier route.

sentences.zh: 騰乃進軍討之，一日下其三城，招納降附者三萬戶。

translations.literal: Teng advanced to attack; in one day he took three walled places and received thirty thousand who surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Teng marched, took three forts in a day, and won thirty thousand submits.

sentences.zh: 帝以騰母在齊，未令東討。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Teng's mother was in Qi, did not yet order an eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was in Qi, so the throne held the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 適有其親屬自齊還朝者，晉公護奏令告騰云：「齊已誅公母兄。

translations.literal: When a kinsman returned from Qi to court, Duke of Jin Hu memorialized to tell Teng: "Qi has already executed your mother and elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman from Qi reported, "Qi killed your mother and brother."

sentences.zh: 」蓋欲發其怒也。

translations.literal: It was meant to stir his rage.
translations.idiomatic: The aim was to stir his rage.

sentences.zh: 騰乃發哀泣血，志在復仇。

translations.literal: Teng then mourned with blood and tears, his will set on revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Teng mourned with blood and vowed revenge.

sentences.zh: 四年，齊公憲與晉公護東征，請騰為副。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Duke Xian of Qi and Duke Hu of Jin campaigned east and asked Teng as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Year 4, Qi and Jin marched east and named Teng deputy.

sentences.zh: 趙公招時在蜀，復欲留之。

translations.literal: Duke Zhao was then in Shu and again wished to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao in Shu again tried to keep him.

sentences.zh: 晉公護與招書，於是令騰馳傳還朝，副憲東伐。

translations.literal: Duke Hu wrote to Zhao; Teng was ordered to ride post-horses back to court and assist Xian in the eastern attack.
translations.idiomatic: Hu wrote Zhao; Teng raced back to join the eastern attack.

sentences.zh: 天和初，信州蠻、蜑據江硤反叛，連結二千餘里，又詔騰討之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe, the Man and Dan of Xin Province held the river gorges and rebelled for more than two thousand li; again Teng was ordered to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Tianhe's start saw Xin Man and Dan hold gorges for two thousand li; Teng was sent.

sentences.zh: 騰沿江南而下，軍至湯口，分道奮擊，所向摧破。

translations.literal: Teng went down the river; when the army reached Tangkou he divided forces and struck; wherever he went, he broke them.
translations.idiomatic: He sailed downriver to Tangkou, split forces, and swept all before him.

sentences.zh: 乃築京觀，以旌武功。

translations.literal: He then built a victory mound to display martial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He raised a victory mound.

sentences.zh: 涪陵郡守蘭休祖又阻兵為亂，方二千餘里。

translations.literal: Fuling Commandery Administrator Lan Xiuzu again raised troops in revolt over two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Fuling's Lan Xiuzu rebelled across two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 復詔騰討之，巴蜀悉定，詔令樹碑紀功績焉。

translations.literal: Again Teng was ordered to attack; Ba and Shu were all settled, and an edict ordered a stele to record his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Teng was sent again; Ba-Shu was settled and a stele ordered.

sentences.zh: 騰自在龍州至是，前後破平諸賊，凡賞得奴婢八百口，馬牛稱是。

translations.literal: From Longzhou until then, Teng had repeatedly broken and pacified the various bandits; in rewards he received eight hundred slaves and concubines and horses and cattle in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: From Longzhou on he had broken every bandit; rewards were eight hundred slaves and herds in proportion.

sentences.zh: 玄字士鑒，入關時，年七歲。

translations.literal: Xuan, styled Shijian, when entering the passes was seven years old.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, styled Shijian, was seven when he entered the passes.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為奉朝請、成平縣令。

translations.literal: In Qi he served as Court Gentleman for the Dynasty and Magistrate of Chengping.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi he was Court Gentleman and Magistrate of Chengping.

sentences.zh: 齊平，武帝見玄，特加勞勉，即拜地官府都上士。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou saw Xuan, treated him with special encouragement, and at once made him Chief Superior Gentleman of the Earth Office.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's fall brought special favor; he became Chief Superior Gentleman of the Earth Office.

sentences.zh: 大象末，為隋文帝相府內兵參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Elephant era he was Internal Military Staff Officer to Chancellor Wen of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: At Elephant's end he was staff officer to Sui's chancellor.

sentences.zh: 玄弟融，字士傾，最知名，少曆顯職。

translations.literal: Xuan's younger brother Rong, styled Shiqing, was the most famous; in youth he held prominent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Younger Rong, styled Shiqing, was most famed and rose young.

sentences.zh: 大象末，位至大將軍、定陵縣公。

translations.literal: At the end of the Elephant era he reached the rank of Grand General and Duke of Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: By Elephant's end he was Grand General and Duke of Dingling.

sentences.zh: 弟麗，少以忠謹，入侍左右，太武特親昵之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Li from youth was loyal and careful, attending at the emperor's side; Taiwu was especially intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Younger Li, loyal from youth, attended Taiwu closely.

sentences.zh: 舉動審慎，初無愆失。

translations.literal: His conduct was cautious; at first he had no fault.
translations.idiomatic: He was careful and faultless at first.

sentences.zh: 賜爵章安子，稍遷南部尚書。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed as Viscount of Zhang'an, he was gradually promoted to Minister of the Southern Court.
translations.idiomatic: Made Viscount of Zhang'an, he rose to Minister of the Southern Court.

sentences.zh: 太武崩，南安王餘立。

translations.literal: When Taiwu died, Prince of Nan'an Yu was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu died; Prince Yu of Nan'an took the throne.

sentences.zh: 既而為中常侍宗愛等所殺。

translations.literal: Soon he was killed by the eunuch Zong Ai and others.
translations.idiomatic: Soon eunuch Zong Ai and others killed him.

sentences.zh: 百寮憂惶，莫知所立。

translations.literal: The hundred officials were anxious and knew not whom to enthrone.
translations.idiomatic: Officials panicked, unsure whom to enthrone.

sentences.zh: 麗首建大議，與殿中尚書長孫渴侯、尚書源賀、羽林中郎劉尼奉迎文成于苑中而立之。

translations.literal: Li was first to propose the great plan; with Palace Director Changsun Kehou, Minister Yuan He, and Feathered Forest Cadet Liu Ni he welcomed Emperor Wencheng from the park and enthroned him.
translations.idiomatic: Li led the plan with Kehou, Yuan He, and Liu Ni to raise Wencheng from the park.

sentences.zh: 社稷獲安，麗之謀也。

translations.literal: The altars were secured—Li's stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was saved by Li's plot.

sentences.zh: 由是受心膂之任，在朝者無出其右。

translations.literal: Hence he received trust at the heart; among those at court none surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: He won the emperor's core trust; none at court matched him.

sentences.zh: 興安初，封平原王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xing'an he was enfeoffed Prince of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At Xing'an he was made Prince of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 麗頻讓，不聽，乃啟以讓父。

translations.literal: Li repeatedly declined and was not heard; he then memorialized to yield to his father.
translations.idiomatic: He declined again and again, then asked to yield to his father.

sentences.zh: 文成曰：「朕為天下主，豈不能得二王封卿父子也？

translations.literal: Wencheng said: "I am lord of all under Heaven—can I not enfeoff father and son as two princes?"
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng said, "Can I not make father and son both princes?"

sentences.zh: 」以其父俟為東平王。

translations.literal: His father Si was made Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: His father Si became Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 麗尋遷侍中、撫軍大將軍、司徒公，復其子孫，賜妻妃號。

translations.literal: Li was soon moved to Attendant, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Duke of the Masses; his descendants were restored, and titles were granted his wife and consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Attendant, Pacifying-Army General, Duke of the Masses; kin restored, consorts titled.

sentences.zh: 麗以優寵既頻，固辭不受，帝益重之。

translations.literal: Because favor came again and again, he firmly declined and would not accept; the emperor esteemed him the more.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated honors he refused; the emperor esteemed him more.

sentences.zh: 領太子太傅。

translations.literal: He held the post of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 麗好學愛士，常以講習為業。

translations.literal: Li loved learning and cherished scholars; he constantly made lecturing his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He loved scholars and lectured constantly.

sentences.zh: 甚孝，遭父憂，毀瘠過禮。

translations.literal: He was very filial; on his father's death his mourning waste exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Filial to excess, his father's mourning broke the rites.

sentences.zh: 和平六年，文成崩。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Heping, Wencheng died.
translations.idiomatic: Heping 6, Wencheng died.

sentences.zh: 先是，麗療疾于代郡溫泉，聞凶欲赴。

translations.literal: Earlier Li had been treating illness at the hot springs in Dai Commandery; hearing the calamity he wished to hurry back.
translations.idiomatic: He was at Dai's hot springs when news came; he raced to return.

sentences.zh: 左右止之曰：「宮車晏駕，王德望素重，奸臣若疾人譽，慮有不測之禍。

translations.literal: Those about him stopped him, saying: "The imperial carriage has just halted; your virtue and fame have long been weighty—if wicked ministers should envy your repute, there may be unforeseen disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Attendants warned, "The throne is empty; your fame may draw traitors."

sentences.zh: 」麗曰：「安有聞君父之喪，方慮禍難！

translations.literal: Li said: "How could one hear of a lord and father's death and still weigh the risk of calamity!"
translations.idiomatic: Li said, "Shall I fear trouble at my father's death?"

sentences.zh: 」便馳赴。

translations.literal: He galloped back at once.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped back.

sentences.zh: 初，乙弗渾悖傲，每為不法，麗數諍之，由是見忌，害之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yifu Hun was arrogant and repeatedly did what was unlawful; Li often remonstrated and therefore was hated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu Hun's arrogance drew Li's remonstrance; Hun killed him.

sentences.zh: 諡曰簡王，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Prince Jian; buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous name Jian; buried at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 孝文追錄先朝功臣，以麗配饗廟庭。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen, recording former-court merit, paired Li in the temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen paired him in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 麗二妻，長曰杜氏，次張氏。

translations.literal: Li had two wives: the elder was the Du clan, the second the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Two wives: Du, then Zhang.

sentences.zh: 長子定國，杜氏所生；

translations.literal: The eldest son Dingguo was born of the Du clan;
translations.idiomatic: Eldest Dingguo was Du's son;

sentences.zh: 次睿，張氏所出。

translations.literal: the second, Rui, was born of the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: second Rui was Zhang's.

sentences.zh: 子昕之，字慶始，風望端雅。

translations.literal: His son Xinzhi, styled Qingshi, had bearing elegant and correct.
translations.idiomatic: Son Xinzhi, styled Qingshi, was grave and elegant.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，例降為公。

translations.literal: He inherited the title; by regulation it was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited, reduced to duke by rule.

sentences.zh: 尚獻文女常山公主，拜駙馬都尉，曆通直郎。

translations.literal: He married Emperor Xianwen's daughter Princess of Changshan and was made Commandant of the Horse Guards and Regular Attendant Direct.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Changshan, became Horse Guards Commandant and Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 景明中，以從叔琇罪，免官。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era, because of cousin Xiu's crime, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingming: cousin Xiu's crime cost him office.

sentences.zh: 尋以主婿，除通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon, as the emperor's son-in-law, he was again made Regular Attendant Direct and Unimpeded.
translations.idiomatic: Soon restored as the emperor's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 曆兗、青二州刺史，並有政績。

translations.literal: He served as Governor of Yan and Qing in succession, both with political achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Yan and Qing with merit.

sentences.zh: 轉安北將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: Transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Made Pacifying-North General and Governor of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈鎮東將軍、冀州刺史，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: At death posthumously General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Ji, posthumous name Hui.
translations.idiomatic: At death posthumously Pacifying-East General and Governor of Ji, posthumous name Hui.

sentences.zh: 初，定國娶河東柳氏，生子安保。

translations.literal: Earlier Dingguo married a woman of the Liu clan of Hedong and had a son Anbao.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo married Liu of Hedong and had Anbao.

sentences.zh: 後娶范陽盧度世女，生昕之。

translations.literal: Later he married a daughter of Lu Dushi of Fanyang and had Xinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he married Lu Dushi's daughter and had Xinzhi.

sentences.zh: 二室俱為舊族，而嫡妾不分。

translations.literal: Both households were old families, yet legitimate wife and concubine were not distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Both were great houses, but wife and concubine were not ranked.

sentences.zh: 定國亡後，兩子爭襲父爵。

translations.literal: After Dingguo died, the two sons contended for their father's title.
translations.idiomatic: After Dingguo's death the sons fought for the title.

sentences.zh: 僕射李沖有寵于時，與度世子伯源婚親相好。

translations.literal: Vice Director Li Chong was favored at the time and was allied by marriage with Dushi's son Boyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Li Chong favored Boyuan, Lu Dushi's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 沖遂左右助之，昕之由是承爵，尚主，職位赫弈。

translations.literal: Chong therefore sided with him, and Xinzhi thereby inherited the title, married the princess, and his posts blazed with glory.
translations.idiomatic: Chong backed Boyuan's side; Xinzhi took the title, the princess, and glory.

sentences.zh: 安保沈廢貧賤，不免饑寒。

translations.literal: Anbao sank into poverty and could not escape cold and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Anbao fell to poverty and hunger.

sentences.zh: 昕之容貌柔謹，孝文以其主婿，特垂昵眷。

translations.literal: Xinzhi's bearing was gentle and careful; Xiaowen, as his son-in-law, showed him special intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle Xinzhi won Xiaowen's special favor as son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，年未四十，頻撫三籓，當世以此榮之。

translations.literal: In the Xuanwu era, before forty, he repeatedly governed the three frontiers—the age counted it glory.
translations.idiomatic: Before forty in Xuanwu's time he held three frontiers—a glory of the age.

sentences.zh: 昕之卒後，母盧悼念，傷過而亡。

translations.literal: After Xinzhi died, his mother Lu grieved until grief killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Mother Lu mourned him to death.

sentences.zh: 公主奉姑有孝稱。

translations.literal: The princess served her mother-in-law with a filial name.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was famed for serving her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 神龜初，與穆氏琅邪長公主並為女侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shengui she and Princess of Langye of the Mu clan were both made Female Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Shengui's start made her and Mu's Langye princess Female Attendants.

sentences.zh: 又性不妒忌，以昕之無子，為納妾媵，而皆育女。

translations.literal: She was also free of jealousy; because Xinzhi had no sons, she took concubines for him, yet all bore daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Without jealousy she took concubines; all bore daughters.

sentences.zh: 公主有三女，無男，以昕之從兄希道第四子子彰為後。

translations.literal: The princess had three daughters and no sons; she took Xinzhi's cousin Xidao's fourth son Zizhang as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Three daughters, no son—she adopted cousin Xidao's fourth son Zizhang.

sentences.zh: 子彰字明遠，本名士沈。

translations.literal: Zizhang, styled Mingyuan, original name Shishen.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhang, styled Mingyuan, born Shishen.

sentences.zh: 年十六出後，事公主盡禮。

translations.literal: At sixteen he left his birth house; toward the princess he fulfilled every rite.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he entered her house and observed every rite.

sentences.zh: 丞相、高陽王雍常言曰：「常山妹雖無男，以子彰為兒，乃過自生矣。

translations.literal: Chancellor Prince Yong of Gaoyang often said: "Though Princess Changshan has no son, taking Zizhang as son surpasses bearing one's own."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong of Gaoyang said, "Adopting Zizhang beats a son of her own."

sentences.zh: 」正光中，襲爵東郡公，累遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era he inherited the title Duke of Dongjun and rose to Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguang: he inherited Duke of Dongjun and rose to Yellow Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 子彰妻即咸陽王禧女。

translations.literal: Zizhang's wife was the daughter of Prince of Xianyang Xi.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was Prince Xi's daughter.

sentences.zh: 禧誅，養于彭城王第，莊帝親之，略同諸姊。

translations.literal: When Xi was executed, she was raised in Prince of Pengcheng's mansion; Emperor Zhuangdi cherished her like his own sisters.
translations.idiomatic: Xi died; she was raised with Pengcheng's daughters, cherished by Zhuangdi.

sentences.zh: 建義初，爾硃榮欲循舊事，庶姓封王，由是封子彰濮陽郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, Erzhu Rong wished to follow old precedent and enfeoff commoners as princes; thus Zizhang was made Prince of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyi: Rong enfeoffed commoners; Zizhang became Prince of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 尋而詔罷，仍復先爵。

translations.literal: Soon an edict revoked it; he returned to his former title.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the edict was revoked.

sentences.zh: 天平中，拜衛將軍、潁州刺史，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he was made Guard General and Governor of Ying; he left office for his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Tianping: Guard General and Governor of Ying; he mourned his mother.

sentences.zh: 元象中，以本將軍除齊州刺史，又加驃騎將軍，行懷州事，轉北豫州刺史，仍除徐州刺史，將軍並如故。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxiang era, with his existing general's title he was made Governor of Qi, then also General of Agile Cavalry acting for Huai, then Governor of Northern Yu, then Governor of Xu—all generals' titles as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxiang: Qi, Agile Cavalry at Huai, Northern Yu, Xu—three provinces in a year.

sentences.zh: 一年曆三州，當世榮之。

translations.literal: One year, three provinces—the age counted it glory.
translations.idiomatic: Three provinces in one year was glory.

sentences.zh: 還朝，除衛大將軍、右光祿大夫，行瀛州事。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was made Guard Grand General and Senior Grand Master of the Splendid, acting for Ying.
translations.idiomatic: At court: Guard Grand General, Senior Splendid Master, acting Ying.

sentences.zh: 尋拜侍中，復行滄州事。

translations.literal: Soon Attendant, again acting for Cang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Attendant, acting Cang.

sentences.zh: 進號驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Advanced in title to General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Agile Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 行冀州事。

translations.literal: Acting for Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Ji.

sentences.zh: 除侍讀，兼七兵尚書，行青州事。

translations.literal: Made Lecturer, concurrently Minister of the Seven Armies, acting for Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Lecturer, Seven Armies Minister, acting Qing.

sentences.zh: 子彰初為州，以聚斂為事，晚節修改，自行青、冀、滄、瀛，甚有時譽。

translations.literal: When Zizhang first held provinces he was grasping; in later years he reformed, and from Qing, Ji, Cang, and Ying he had great contemporary praise.
translations.idiomatic: Early greed gave way to reform; Qing, Ji, Cang, and Ying won praise.

sentences.zh: 加以虛己納物，人士敬愛之。

translations.literal: He also received others with empty humility; gentlemen revered and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Humble toward others, he was loved by gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 除中書監。

translations.literal: Made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: At death posthumously Commissioner with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, posthumous name Wensuan.
translations.idiomatic: At death posthumously Commissioner, posthumous name Wensuan.

sentences.zh: 子彰崇好道術，曾嬰重病藥中須桑螵蛸。

translations.literal: Zizhang deeply loved Daoist arts; once gravely ill, his medicine needed praying mantis egg-cases.
translations.idiomatic: He loved Daoism; grave illness needed mantis egg-cases in medicine.

sentences.zh: 子彰不忍害物，遂不服焉，其仁如此。

translations.literal: Zizhang could not bear to harm living things and therefore did not take the medicine—such was his benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: He would not harm creatures and refused the dose—such was his kindness.

sentences.zh: 教訓六子，雅有法度。

translations.literal: He taught six sons with elegant discipline.
translations.idiomatic: He trained six sons with strict grace.

sentences.zh: 子仰。

translations.literal: His son Yang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yang.

sentences.zh: 仰字雲駒，少機悟，美風神。

translations.literal: Yang, styled Yunju, was clever from youth with fine spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Yang, styled Yunju, was quick and fine-spirited.

sentences.zh: 好學不倦，博覽群書，《五經》多通大義。

translations.literal: He loved learning without tiring, read widely, and penetrated the great meaning of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely and grasped the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，甚為河間邢邵所賞。

translations.literal: Skilled at composition, he was greatly prized by Xing Shao of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shao of Hejian prized his writing.

sentences.zh: 劭又與子彰交遊，嘗謂子彰曰：「吾以卿老蜯遂出明珠，意欲為群拜紀可乎？

translations.literal: Shao also befriended Zizhang and once told him: "From your old oyster I drew forth a pearl—shall I have the crowd bow to the chronicle?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao told Zizhang, "From your oyster came a pearl—shall I have men bow to the chronicle?"

sentences.zh: 」由是名譽日高，雅為搢紳所推許。

translations.literal: Hence his fame rose daily and gentlemen of the girdle praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Fame rose; gentry praised him.

sentences.zh: 起家員外散騎侍郎，曆文襄大將軍主簿、中書舍人、兼中書侍郎，以本職兼太子洗馬。

translations.literal: He began as Supernumerary Regular Attendant, then Secretariat Chief Clerk to Grand General Wenxiang, Secretariat Attendant, concurrent Secretariat Vice Director, and in his existing office concurrently Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from attendant to Wenxiang's clerk, Secretariat posts, and Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 自梁、魏通和，歲有交聘，仰每兼官宴接。

translations.literal: From Liang and Wei exchanging envoys each year, Yang often jointly received banquets.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang and Wei exchanged envoys, Yang often hosted banquets.

sentences.zh: 在席賦詩，仰必先成，雖未能盡工，以敏速見美。

translations.literal: At the feast composing poems, Yang always finished first; though not fully polished, he was praised for speed.
translations.idiomatic: At feasts he finished poems first—praised for speed if not polish.

sentences.zh: 除中書侍郎，修國史。

translations.literal: Made Secretariat Vice Director and edited the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Vice Director editing national history.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office for his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his father.

sentences.zh: 居喪盡禮，哀毀骨立，詔以本官起。

translations.literal: In mourning he fulfilled every rite; grief wasted him to bone; an edict recalled him in his existing office.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning broke his body; edict recalled him.

sentences.zh: 文襄時鎮鄴，嘉其至行，親詣門以慰勉之。

translations.literal: When Grand General Wenxiang was stationed at Ye, he prized this utmost conduct and came in person to his gate to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang at Ye came himself to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 仰母，魏上庸公主。

translations.literal: Yang's mother was Princess of Shangyong of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Wei's Princess of Shangyong.

sentences.zh: 初封藍田，高明婦人也。

translations.literal: First enfeoffed as Princess of Lantian—a woman of high clarity.
translations.idiomatic: First Princess of Lantian—a woman of clarity.

sentences.zh: 甚有志操。

translations.literal: She had great resolve.
translations.idiomatic: She had strong resolve.

sentences.zh: 仰昆季六人，並主所出，故邢邵常謂人云：「藍田生玉，固不虛矣。

translations.literal: Yang's six brothers were all born of the princess; therefore Xing Shao often told people: "Lantian bears jade—indeed not empty praise."
translations.idiomatic: Six brothers all her sons—Shao said, "Lantian bears jade—not empty fame."

sentences.zh: 」主教訓諸子，皆以義方。

translations.literal: The princess taught her sons all by righteous rule.
translations.idiomatic: She taught her sons righteousness.

sentences.zh: 雖創巨痛深，出於天性；

translations.literal: Though the wound was vast and grief deep, springing from inborn nature;
translations.idiomatic: Grief vast as nature,

sentences.zh: 然動依禮度，亦母氏之訓焉。

translations.literal: yet in movement he kept within ritual bounds—that too was his mother's instruction.
translations.idiomatic: yet he kept within ritual—his mother's teaching.

sentences.zh: 仰兄弟相率廬于墓側，負土成墳。

translations.literal: Yang's brothers led one another in building huts beside the tomb, carrying earth to form the grave mound.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers camped together by the grave and piled earth into a mound.

sentences.zh: 朝廷所嗟尚，發詔褒揚，改其所居裏為孝終裏。

translations.literal: What the court admired in Yang was issued in an edict of praise; his residential lane was renamed Filial-End Lane.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended him by edict and renamed his neighborhood Filial-End Lane.

sentences.zh: 服竟，當襲，不忍嗣侯。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was due to inherit; he could not bear to succeed as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he should have taken the marquisate, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 使迄未應受。

translations.literal: The envoy in the end never accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: He never did accept the title.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，常山王薦仰器幹，文宣面授給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In early Qi Tianbao the Prince of Changshan recommended Yang's ability; Wensuan personally appointed him Attendant of the Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tianbao the Prince of Changshan recommended Yang, and Emperor Wensuan personally made him Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 上洛王思宗為清都尹，辟為邑中正，食貝丘縣幹。

translations.literal: Sizong, Prince of Shangluo, was Qingdu Intendant; Yang was recruited as chief of the district and drew salary as a Beiqiu county officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Sizong of Shangluo served as Qingdu intendant, he made Yang district chief with a stipend from Beiqiu.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，哀慕毀悴，殆不勝喪，遂至沈篤，頓伏床枕，又成風疾。

translations.literal: He suffered his mother's death; grief and longing wasted him, nearly unable to bear mourning; it reached grave illness, prostrate on bed and pillow, and he also developed wind ailment.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died he grieved until he nearly collapsed; he lay bedridden and developed a wind disorder.

sentences.zh: 第五弟摶遇疾，臨終，謂其兄弟曰：「大兄尪病如此，性至慈愛，摶之死日，必不得使大兄知之，哭泣聲必不可聞徹，致有感動。

translations.literal: His fifth younger brother Bo fell ill; at the end he told his brothers: "Elder brother is so frail and ill, by nature utterly loving; on the day of Bo's death you must not let elder brother know; sounds of weeping must not be heard penetrating, lest it move him."
translations.idiomatic: His fifth brother Bo, dying, told the family: "Our eldest is frail and tender-hearted—when I die he must not hear it; no weeping must reach him or it will break him."

sentences.zh: 」家人至於祖載，方始告之。

translations.literal: " The family only at the ancestral procession told him.
translations.idiomatic: The family told him only when the funeral cortege set out.

sentences.zh: 仰聞而悲痛，一慟便絕。

translations.literal: When Yang heard it he grieved in anguish; one sob and he expired.
translations.idiomatic: Yang heard and sobbed once—and died.

sentences.zh: 年四十八。

translations.literal: Age forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 仰自在朝行，篤慎周密。

translations.literal: Yang from his time in court ranks was earnest, cautious, and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: In office Yang was earnest, careful, and meticulous.

sentences.zh: 不說人短，不伐己長，言論清遠，有人倫鑒裁，朝野甚悲惜之。

translations.literal: He did not speak of others' faults, did not boast of his own strengths; discourse was clear and far-reaching; he had judgment of human relations; court and countryside deeply mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: He never gossiped about faults or trumpeted his gifts; his speech was measured and discerning, and all who knew him grieved.

sentences.zh: 贈衛將軍、青州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded General of the Guards and Governor of Qingzhou; posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General of the Guards and Governor of Qingzhou, with the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 所著文章十四卷，行於世。

translations.literal: Writings in fourteen scrolls circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen scrolls of his writings circulated.

sentences.zh: 齊之郊廟諸歌，多仰所制。

translations.literal: Many of Qi's suburban and temple songs were composed by Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Northern Qi's temple and suburban hymns were Yang's work.

sentences.zh: 子乂字旦，襲爵始平侯。

translations.literal: His son Yi, styled Dan, inherited the marquisate of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi, styled Dan, took the marquisate of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 乂聰敏博學，有文才，年十九舉司州秀才。

translations.literal: Yi was clever, keen, broadly learned, with literary talent; at nineteen he was nominated Qi prefectural outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and widely read, Yi showed literary talent and at nineteen was nominated prefectural outstanding talent.

sentences.zh: 曆秘書郎、南陽王文學、通直散騎侍郎，待詔文林館，兼散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He passed through Secretariat Gentleman, Literary Scholar to the Prince of Nanyang, and Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry; he awaited orders at the Wulin Hall and concurrently served as Regular Cavalry Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as secretariat gentleman, literary scholar to the Prince of Nanyang, and regular attendant of the unimpeded cavalry, awaiting orders at the Wulin Hall.

sentences.zh: 迎陳使，還，兼中書舍人，加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Receiving the Chen envoy, on return he was concurrently Secretariat Drafter and added Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving a Chen envoy he was also made secretariat drafter and regular attendant of the unimpeded cavalry.

sentences.zh: 乂於《五經》最精熟，館中謂之石經。

translations.literal: Yi was most expert in the Five Classics; in the hall they called him the Stone Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Yi knew the Five Classics best; colleagues called him the living Stone Classics.

sentences.zh: 人為之語曰：「《五經》無對，有陸乂。」

translations.literal: People made a saying: "The Five Classics have no match—there is Lu Yi."
translations.idiomatic: A saying ran: "No one matches him on the Five Classics—there is Lu Yi."

sentences.zh: 仰第二弟駿，字雲驤。

translations.literal: Yang's second younger brother Jun, styled Yunxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang's second brother Jun, styled Yunxiang.

sentences.zh: 自中書舍人曆黃門侍郎、散騎常侍，卒于東廣州刺史。

translations.literal: From Secretariat Drafter he passed through Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate and Regular Attendant; he died as Governor of Eastern Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from secretariat drafter through the yellow gate to regular attendant and died as governor of Eastern Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 駿弟杳，字雲邁，亦曆中書舍人、黃門常侍，假儀同三司、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Jun's younger brother Yao, styled Yunmai, also passed through Secretariat Drafter and Regular Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate; provisionally Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes and Governor of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's brother Yao, styled Yunmai, held the same court posts and served provisionally as equal to the three dukes and governor of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 武平中，為寇所圍。

translations.literal: In Wuping he was besieged by raiders.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuping raiders besieged his city.

sentences.zh: 經百餘日，就加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: After more than a hundred days he was promoted to Grand Guardian Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: After a hundred-odd days he was made grand guardian equal to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 城中多疫癘，死者過半，人無異心。

translations.literal: In the city plague was rife; more than half died; the people had no divided hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Plague killed more than half the city, yet morale never cracked.

sentences.zh: 遇疾卒。

translations.literal: He fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，陳將吳明徹以杳有善政，吏人所懷，啟陳主，還其屍，家累貲物無所犯。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the Chen general Wu Mingche, because Yao had good government and officials and people cherished him, reported to the Chen ruler and returned his corpse; family and accumulated goods were not violated.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Wu Mingche of Chen, honoring Yao's good rule, had his body returned unharmed and forbade looting.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司、尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Grand Guardian Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes and Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand guardian equal to the three dukes and vice minister of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 子玄卿，位尚書膳部郎。

translations.literal: His son Xuanqing held the post of Gentleman of the Masters of Writing for Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuanqing was gentleman of the masters of writing for provisions.

sentences.zh: 杳弟騫，字雲儀，亦曆中書舍人、黃門常侍。

translations.literal: Yao's younger brother Qian, styled Yunyi, also passed through Secretariat Drafter and Regular Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's brother Qian, styled Yunyi, also served as secretariat drafter and regular gentleman of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 武平末，吏部郎中。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping he was Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he directed the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 騫弟摶，字雲征，好學有行檢，卒于著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Qian's younger brother Bo, styled Yunzheng, loved learning and had conduct and restraint; he died as Assistant in the Bureau of Writings.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's brother Bo, styled Yunzheng, was studious and upright and died as assistant in the bureau of writings.

sentences.zh: 摶弟彥師，字雲房，少以行檢稱。

translations.literal: Bo's younger brother Yan Shi, styled Yunfang, was known in youth for conduct and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's brother Yan Shi, styled Yunfang, was known young for integrity.

sentences.zh: 及長好學，解屬文。

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning and understood regulated prose.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he studied hard and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 魏襄城王元旭引為參軍事，以父艱去職。

translations.literal: Yuan Xu, Prince of Xiangcheng of Wei, brought him in as military aide; he left office on his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiangcheng Yuan Xu took him as aide; he left office when his father died.

sentences.zh: 哀毀殆不勝喪，與兄仰廬于墓次。

translations.literal: Grief and ruin nearly unbearable for mourning; with his brother Yang he built huts at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Grief nearly destroyed him; he camped at the tomb with his brother Yang.

sentences.zh: 鄉人重之，皆就墓側存問；

translations.literal: The villagers esteemed them and all came to the tomb side to inquire after them;
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors honored them and flocked to the graveside to console them;

sentences.zh: 晦朔之際，車馬不絕。

translations.literal: at new and full moon, carriages and horses were unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: on every new and full moon the road was never empty of visitors.

sentences.zh: 中書令河間邢邵表薦之。

translations.literal: Chief Secretariat Xing Shao of Hejian memorialized to recommend him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Secretariat Xing Shao of Hejian recommended him by memorial.

sentences.zh: 未報，彭城王浟為司州牧，召補主簿。

translations.literal: Before a reply, the Prince of Pengcheng You as Governor of Sizhou summoned him to supplement as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Before the court answered, You, Prince of Pengcheng and governor of Sizhou, made him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 後曆中外府東閣祭酒。

translations.literal: Later he passed through Eastern Attendant of the Inner and Outer Offices.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as eastern attendant in the inner and outer offices.

sentences.zh: 兄仰當襲父始平侯，以彥師昆弟中最幼，表讓封焉，彥師固辭而止。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yang was due to inherit their father's marquisate of Shiping; because Yan Shi was youngest among the brothers he memorialized to yield the fief to him; Yan Shi firmly declined and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Yang was to inherit Shiping; he tried to yield to the youngest, Yan Shi, who refused and the matter ended.

sentences.zh: 世稱友悌孝義，總萃一門。

translations.literal: The age praised friendship, fraternal duty, and filial righteousness gathered in one clan.
translations.idiomatic: The age praised their fraternal bond and filial piety as unrivaled in one house.

sentences.zh: 為中書舍人、通直散騎侍郎。
