translations.literal: He was Secretariat Drafter and Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He became secretariat drafter and regular attendant of the unimpeded cavalry.

sentences.zh: 每陳使至，必高選主客，彥師所接對者，前後六輩。

translations.literal: Whenever Chen envoys arrived, the chief guest was always chosen with care; those Yan Shi received numbered six parties in all.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Chen envoys came, the court picked its best host—Yan Shi entertained six missions in succession.

sentences.zh: 曆中書、黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He passed through Secretariat and Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the secretariat and as gentleman of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 後以不阿宦者，遇讒，出為中山太守，有惠政。

translations.literal: Later because he would not flatter eunuchs he met slander and was sent out as Governor of Zhongshan; he had benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: Later, refusing to court eunuchs, he was slandered out to Zhongshan, where he ruled with kindness.

sentences.zh: 數年，徵為吏部郎中、散騎常侍，又拜銀青光祿大夫，假儀同三司，行鄭州刺史，尋除給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Several years later he was summoned as Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Regular Attendant; he was also appointed Grand Master of Splendid Glory with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon, provisionally Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, acting Governor of Zhengzhou; soon removed as Attendant of the Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he returned as personnel director and regular attendant, then silver-seal grand master acting equal to the three dukes and governor of Zhengzhou, soon gentleman of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 武平末，車駕如晉陽，北平王鎮鄴，委彥師留台機密，以重慎見知。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping the imperial carriage went to Jinyang; the Prince of Northern Ping garrisoned Ye; Yan Shi was entrusted with capital secrets, known for weighty caution.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Jinyang and the Prince of Northern Ping held Ye, Yan Shi was left with capital secrets, trusted for his caution.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊，授彥師下大夫，轉少納言，賜爵臨水縣男。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi he appointed Yan Shi junior grand master and transferred him to junior admonisher; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Linshui.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou's conquest of Qi he made Yan Shi junior grand master and junior admonisher, baron of Linshui.

sentences.zh: 及隋文為丞相，彥師遇疾，請假還鄴。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chancellor, Yan Shi fell ill and asked leave to return to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen of Sui was still chancellor, Yan Shi fell ill and went home to Ye.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥將為亂，彥師知之，遂將妻子潛歸長安。

translations.literal: Yu Chi Jiong was about to rebel; Yan Shi knew it and secretly took wife and children back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Yu Chi Jiong would rebel, he slipped his family back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘉之，授內史下大夫，拜上儀同。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen praised this and appointed him junior grand master of the Palace Secretariat and awarded Upper Equal in Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wen praised him, made him junior grand master of the palace secretariat, and gave him upper equal rank.

sentences.zh: 及帝受禪，拜尚書左丞，進爵為子。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the abdication he was appointed Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing on the left and advanced in rank to viscount.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Sui he became left vice minister of the masters of writing and was raised to viscount.

sentences.zh: 彥師素多病，未幾，以務劇病動，乞解所職，有詔聽以本官就第。

translations.literal: Yan Shi had long been often ill; before long, duties being heavy his illness stirred; he begged to be relieved of office; an edict allowed him to keep his rank at home.
translations.idiomatic: Chronically ill, he soon asked to quit when heavy duties worsened his health; the throne let him keep rank at home.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became vice director of personnel.

sentences.zh: 隋承周制，官無清濁，彥師在職，凡所任人，頗甄別於士庶，論者美之。

translations.literal: Sui inherited Zhou's system; offices had no pure or base distinction; Yan Shi in office, for all he appointed, quite distinguished gentry from commoners; commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Sui kept Zhou's offices without "pure" versus "base" ranks; Yan Shi still distinguished gentry from commoners in appointments, to general praise.

sentences.zh: 後復以病出為汾州刺史，卒官。

translations.literal: Later again because of illness he went out as Governor of Fenzhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Ill again, he went out as governor of Fenzhou and died there.

sentences.zh: 睿字思弼，年十餘，襲爵撫軍大將軍、平原王。

translations.literal: Rui, styled Sibi, in his teens inherited the rank General Who Pacifies the Army and Prince of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Rui, styled Sibi, inherited at barely ten as General Who Pacifies the Army and Prince of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 沈雅好學，折節下士。

translations.literal: Deeply refined, he loved learning and bent his will to honor scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Refined and bookish, he humbled himself before scholars.

sentences.zh: 年未二十，時人便以宰輔許之。

translations.literal: Before twenty, people of the time already promised him the highest ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Before twenty contemporaries already called him a future chief minister.

sentences.zh: 娶東徐州刺史博陵崔鑒女。

translations.literal: He married the daughter of Cui Jian, Governor of Eastern Xuzhou of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: He married Cui Jian of Boling, governor of Eastern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時孝文尚未改北人姓，鑒謂所親云：「平原王才度不惡，但恨其姓名殊為重復。

translations.literal: At the time Xiaowen had not yet changed northern surnames; Jian told those close: "The Prince of Pingyuan's talent and measure are not bad, but I regret his name is quite redundantly repeated."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen had not yet sinicized names; Jian said to friends, "The prince has talent, but that name of his is painfully repetitive."

sentences.zh: 」睿婚，自東徐還經鄴，見李彪，甚敬悅之。

translations.literal: " On Rui's marriage, returning from Eastern Xu through Ye, he met Li Biao and deeply respected and delighted in him.
translations.idiomatic: On his wedding journey home through Ye he met Li Biao and took an immediate liking to him.

sentences.zh: 仍與趣京，以為館客。

translations.literal: He then went with him to the capital and made him a hall guest.
translations.idiomatic: He brought Biao to the capital as a household guest.

sentences.zh: 後為北征都督，擊蠕蠕，大破之。

translations.literal: Later he was commander of the northern expedition, struck the Rouran, and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as northern expedition commander, he routed the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、都曹尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant and Master of Writing for All Offices.
translations.idiomatic: He became palace attendant and master of writing for all offices.

sentences.zh: 時蠕蠕又犯塞，詔睿討之，追至石磧，禽其帥赤阿突等數百人。

translations.literal: At the time the Rouran again violated the frontier; an edict ordered Rui to attack; pursuing to Shiji, he captured their chieftain Chi'atou and several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran raided again, Rui pursued them to Shiji and took their chief Chi'atou and hundreds of captives.

sentences.zh: 還，加散騎常侍，遷尚書左僕射，領北部尚書。

translations.literal: On return he was added Regular Attendant and transferred to Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing on the Left, heading the Northern Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he was made regular attendant and left vice minister, heading the northern masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 十六年，降五等之爵，以麗勳著前朝，封睿钜鹿郡公。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the five-rank noble ranks were lowered; because Li's merit shone in the former dynasty, Rui was enfeoffed Duke of Julu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen ranks were trimmed; for Li's old merit Rui was made Duke of Julu.

sentences.zh: 尋為使持節、鎮北大將軍、尚書令、衛將軍，討蠕蠕，大破之而還。

translations.literal: Soon he was Bearer of the Staff, Grand General Who Pacifies the North, Master of Writing, and General of the Guards; he campaigned against the Rouran, greatly defeated them, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, staff-bearing grand general who pacifies the north, master of writing, and guards general, he smashed the Rouran again.

sentences.zh: 以母憂解。

translations.literal: He resigned on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office for his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 孝文將有南伐之事，以本官起授征南將軍。

translations.literal: Xiaowen was about to undertake a southern campaign; with his former rank he was recalled and appointed General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowen planned a southern war he was recalled as General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 睿固辭，請終情禮，敕有司敦喻不許。

translations.literal: Rui firmly declined, asking to complete the mourning rites; an edict ordered the offices earnestly to instruct him and would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Rui refused, pleading to finish mourning; the throne ordered him back and would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 復除使持節、都督恆州刺史，行尚書令。

translations.literal: He was again removed as Bearer of the Staff and Area Commander of Hengzhou, acting Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made staff-bearer and area commander of Hengzhou, acting master of writing.

sentences.zh: 時車駕南征，上表諫，帝不從。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial carriage was on southern campaign; he memorialized to remonstrate; the emperor did not heed.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor marched south he memorialized in protest; the emperor ignored him.

sentences.zh: 睿又表請車駕還代，親臨太師馮熙葬，坐削奪都督三州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Rui again memorialized asking the imperial carriage to return to Dai and personally attend Grand Tutor Feng Xi's funeral; he was punished by stripping Area Commander of the Three Provinces and all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the emperor to return for Feng Xi's funeral and lost command of three provinces' armies.

sentences.zh: 尋進號征北大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon his title was advanced to Grand General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to grand general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 以有順遷之表，加邑四百戶。

translations.literal: Because he had a memorial favoring transfer of the capital, his fief was increased by four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: A memorial favoring the capital move won him four hundred added households.

sentences.zh: 時穆泰為定州刺史，以疾病，請恆州自效，乃以睿為定州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time Mu Tai was Governor of Dingzhou; because of illness he asked to serve at Hengzhou; Rui was then made Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Tai of Dingzhou, ill, asked to swap to Hengzhou; Rui replaced him at Ding.

sentences.zh: 未發，遂與泰等同謀構逆，賜死獄中。

translations.literal: Before he set out, he then with Tai and others alike plotted rebellion; he was granted death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Before he marched he plotted with Mu Tai and others; he was ordered to die in prison.

sentences.zh: 聽免孥戮，徙其妻子于遼西。

translations.literal: His wife and children were spared collective execution and were relocated to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: His family was spared the clan penalty and exiled to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 睿長子希道，字洪度。

translations.literal: Rui's eldest son Xidao, styled Hongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's eldest son Xidao, styled Hongdu.

sentences.zh: 有風貌，美須髯，曆覽經史，頗有文致。

translations.literal: He had bearing and grace, a fine beard; he ranged through the classics and histories and had quite literary polish.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome, bearded, well read, he wrote with some elegance.

sentences.zh: 初拜中散，遷通直郎。

translations.literal: At first appointed Palace Scribe; transferred to Unimpeded Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He began as palace scribe and became unimpeded gentleman.

sentences.zh: 坐父事，徙於遼西。

translations.literal: Because of his father's affair he was relocated to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his father's crime he was exiled to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 于後得還，從征自效，以軍功賜爵淮陽男，拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was able to return; following campaigns he offered his effort; for military merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Huaiyang and appointed Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Later restored, he earned merit on campaign and was made baron of Huaiyang and remonstrating grand master.

sentences.zh: 累遷前將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Forward General and Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to forward general and governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 希道善於馭邊，甚有威略。

translations.literal: Xidao was skilled at controlling the frontier and had great martial strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Xidao governed the frontier well and was a formidable strategist.

sentences.zh: 轉平西將軍、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became general who pacifies the west and governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈撫軍將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumously awarded General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously made general who pacifies the army and governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 希道有六子：士懋字元偉。

translations.literal: Xidao had six sons: Shimao, styled Yuanwei.
translations.idiomatic: Xidao had six sons; the eldest was Shimao, styled Yuanwei.

sentences.zh: 天平中以其曾祖麗有翼戴之勳，詔特復钜鹿郡公，令士懋襲。

translations.literal: In Tianping, because his great-grandfather Li had merit in supporting and establishing the ruler, an edict specially restored the Duke of Julu commandery and ordered Shimao to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping, for great-grandfather Li's role enthroning the emperor, Shimao was restored to the Julu dukedom.

sentences.zh: 位營州刺史。

translations.literal: He held the post of Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 士懋弟士宗，字仲彥，尚書左外兵郎中。

translations.literal: Shimao's younger brother Shizong, styled Zhongyan, was Gentleman of the Masters of Writing for Outer Troops on the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Shimao's brother Shizong, styled Zhongyan, was left gentleman of the masters of writing for outer troops.

sentences.zh: 士宗弟士述，字幼文，符璽郎中。

translations.literal: Shizong's younger brother Shishu, styled Youwen, was Gentleman of the Masters of Writing for Seals and Credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong's brother Shishu, styled Youwen, was gentleman for seals and credentials.

sentences.zh: 建義初，並于河陰遇害。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi both were killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: In early Jianyi both were killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 士述弟士沈，出繼叔昕之。

translations.literal: Shishu's younger brother Shishen was given in succession to his uncle Xinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shishu's brother Shishen was adopted by his uncle Xinzhi.

sentences.zh: 士沈弟士廉，字季脩，建州平北府長史。

translations.literal: Shishen's younger brother Shilian, styled Jixiu, was Chief Clerk of the Pingbei Headquarters of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shishen's brother Shilian, styled Jixiu, was chief clerk of Jianzhou's pingbei headquarters.

sentences.zh: 永安末，爾硃世隆攻陷州城，見害。

translations.literal: At the end of Yong'an Erzhu Shilong stormed and took the prefectural city; he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Shilong took Jianzhou at the end of Yong'an, Shilian was killed.

sentences.zh: 士廉弟士佩，字季偉，武定中，安東將軍、司州從事。

translations.literal: Shilian's younger brother Shipei, styled Jiwei, in Wuding was General Who Pacifies the East and Retainer of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian's brother Shipei, styled Jiwei, in Wuding was general who pacifies the east and Sizhou retainer.

sentences.zh: 希道弟希悅，尚書外兵郎中。

translations.literal: Xidao's younger brother Xiyue was Gentleman of the Masters of Writing for Outer Troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xidao's brother Xiyue was gentleman of the masters of writing for outer troops.

sentences.zh: 麗季弟騏驎，侍御中散，轉侍御史。

translations.literal: Li's younger brother Qilin was Palace Attendant Within the Hall and Scribe, transferred to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Li's younger brother Qilin was palace attendant within the hall, then attending censor.

sentences.zh: 太和初，新平太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was Governor of Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: In early Taihe he governed Xinping.

sentences.zh: 子高貴，孝昌中，兗州鎮東府法曹參軍。

translations.literal: His son Gaogui in Xiaochang was Legal Bureau Aide of the Eastern Garrison Headquarters of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gaogui in Xiaochang was legal aide on Yanzhou's eastern staff.

sentences.zh: 高貴子操，字仲志，高簡有風格，早以學業知名，雅好文。

translations.literal: Gaogui's son Cao, styled Zhongzhi, was lofty, simple, and had style; early he was known for scholarship and elegantly loved literature.
translations.idiomatic: Gaogui's son Cao, styled Zhongzhi, was austere and stylish, famed early for learning and fond of letters.

sentences.zh: 操仕魏，兼散騎常侍聘梁。

translations.literal: Cao served Wei as Concurrent Regular Attendant on an embassy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao of Wei served as concurrent regular attendant on an embassy to Liang.

sentences.zh: 使還，為廷尉卿。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned he was Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he became minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄為世子，甚好色，崔季舒為掌媒焉。

translations.literal: Qi Wenxiang as heir was very fond of women; Cui Jishu was in charge of matchmaking.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang of Qi, as heir apparent, was licentious; Cui Jishu arranged his affairs.

sentences.zh: 薛氏寘書妻元氏有色，迎入欲通之。

translations.literal: Xue Zhi's wife Yuan of the Registrar's office was beautiful in color; she was brought in and he wished to have relations with her.
translations.idiomatic: He brought in Yuan, wife of Registrar Xue Zhi, intending to take her.

sentences.zh: 元氏正辭，且哭。

translations.literal: Yuan spoke uprightly and also wept.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan rebuked him sternly and wept.

sentences.zh: 世子使季舒送付廷尉罪之。

translations.literal: The heir sent Jishu to deliver her to the Court of Justice to punish her.
translations.idiomatic: The heir had Jishu send her to justice for punishment.

sentences.zh: 操曰：「廷尉守天子法，須知罪狀。

translations.literal: Cao said: "The Minister of Justice guards the Son of Heaven's law; he must know the crime."
translations.idiomatic: Cao said, "Justice guards the emperor's law—we must know the charge."

sentences.zh: 」世子怒，召操，命刀環築之，更令科罪。

translations.literal: " The heir was angry, summoned Cao, ordered the ring of the blade to strike him, and again ordered conviction.
translations.idiomatic: The heir raged, had him beaten with a sword-ring, and demanded a verdict.

sentences.zh: 操終不撓，乃口責之。

translations.literal: Cao to the end did not bend; then he reproached him orally.
translations.idiomatic: Cao never yielded and rebuked him to his face.

sentences.zh: 後徙御史中丞。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Censor in Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made censor in chief.

sentences.zh: 天保中，卒于殿中尚書。

translations.literal: In Tianbao he died as Director Within the Hall of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao he died as director within the hall of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 子孔璋，武平中，卒于高陽太守。

translations.literal: His son Kongzhang in Wuping died as Governor of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kongzhang died in Wuping as governor of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 高貴弟孟遠，位奉朝請。

translations.literal: Gaogui's younger brother Mengyuan held the post of Court Gentleman for the Dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Gaogui's brother Mengyuan was a court gentleman for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 孟遠子概之，位司農卿。

translations.literal: Mengyuan's son Gaizhi held the post of Minister of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyuan's son Gaizhi was minister of the imperial granaries.

sentences.zh: 概之子爽，字開明。

translations.literal: Gaizhi's son Shuang, styled Kaiming.
translations.idiomatic: Gaizhi's son Shuang, styled Kaiming.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏，年九歲就學，日誦二千餘言。

translations.literal: In youth clever and keen; at nine he entered study; each day he recited more than two thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: Clever as a boy, at nine he recited over two thousand characters a day.

sentences.zh: 齊尚書僕射楊遵彥見而異之曰：「陸氏世有人焉。

translations.literal: Yang Zunyan, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing of Qi, saw him and marveled, saying: "The Lu clan always produces men."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zunyan, Qi vice minister of the masters of writing, said in wonder, "The Lus never run dry of talent."

sentences.zh: 」仕齊，位中書侍郎。

translations.literal: " He served Qi as Secretariat Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He served Qi as secretariat vice minister.

sentences.zh: 齊滅，周武帝聞其名，與陽休之、袁叔德等俱征入關。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou heard his name and with Yang Xiuzhi, Yuan Shude, and others alike was summoned into the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell, Zhou's emperor summoned him with Yang Xiuzhi and Yuan Shude into the Pass.

sentences.zh: 諸人多將輜重，爽獨載數千卷書。

translations.literal: Many brought heavy baggage; Shuang alone loaded several thousand scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: Others hauled valuables; Shuang brought only thousands of scrolls.

sentences.zh: 至長安，授宣納上士。

translations.literal: Reaching Chang'an he was appointed Upper Gentleman for Proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an he was made upper gentleman for proclamation.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，頻遷太子洗馬，與左庶子宇文愷等撰《東宮典記》七十卷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication he was repeatedly promoted to Crown Prince Reader; with Left Heir Apparent Yuwen Kai and others he compiled seventy scrolls of Records of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui he rose to crown prince reader and with Yuwen Kai compiled seventy scrolls of Eastern Palace records.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其博學有口辯，陳人至境，常令迎勞。

translations.literal: The court because of his broad learning and eloquence, whenever Chen people reached the border, always ordered him to welcome and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: His learning and tongue made him the court's choice to greet Chen envoys at the border.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈上儀同、宣州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumously awarded Upper Equal in Rank and Governor of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office, posthumously upper equal in rank and governor of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 子法言，敏學有家風，釋褐承奉郎。

translations.literal: His son Fayin, keen in learning with family style, on first appointment was Gentleman for Reception.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fayin, quick-witted and true to the family trade, began as gentleman for reception.

sentences.zh: 初，爽之為洗馬，常奏文帝云：「皇太子諸子未有嘉名，請依《春秋》之義，更立名字。

translations.literal: At first when Shuang was reader he often memorialized to Emperor Wen: "The crown prince's sons have no fine names; I ask according to the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals to establish new names."
translations.idiomatic: As reader, Shuang asked Wen to rename the crown prince's sons by Spring and Autumn precedent.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 及太子廢，上追怒爽曰：「我孫制名，甯不自解？

translations.literal: When the crown prince was deposed the emperor pursued anger at Shuang, saying: "My grandsons' names—would I not understand them myself?"
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince fell, Wen raged at Shuang: "Did I need him to name my grandsons?"

sentences.zh: 陸爽乃爾多事！

translations.literal: Lu Shuang is so meddlesome!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang meddled once too often!

sentences.zh: 扇惑於勇，亦由此人。

translations.literal: Inciting Yong also began with this man.
translations.idiomatic: He also stirred up Yong.

sentences.zh: 其身雖故，子孫並宜屏黜，終身不齒。

translations.literal: Though his person is gone, descendants should all be screened and dismissed, never counted among the ranks for life.
translations.idiomatic: Though dead, his line should be erased from office forever.

sentences.zh: 」法言竟坐除名。

translations.literal: " Fayin in the end was punished by removal of name.
translations.idiomatic: Fayin was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 源賀，西平樂都人，私署河西王禿發傉檀之子也。

translations.literal: Yuan He, a native of Ledu in Xiping, was son of Tufa Rutan, self-styled King of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan He of Ledu in Xiping was son of Tufa Rutan, the self-styled King of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 傉檀為乞伏熾盤所滅，賀自樂都奔魏。

translations.literal: Rutan was destroyed by Qifu Chitan; He fled from Ledu to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Chitan of Qifu destroyed Rutan, He fled to Wei from Ledu.

sentences.zh: 賀偉容貌，善風儀。

translations.literal: He had grand appearance and was skilled in bearing and deportment.
translations.idiomatic: He was imposing and graceful in manner.

sentences.zh: 太武素聞其名。

translations.literal: Taiwu had long heard his name.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu had long known his name.

sentences.zh: 及見，器其機辯，賜爵西平侯。

translations.literal: When he saw him he valued his quick wit in debate and enfeoffed him Marquis of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting him, the emperor prized his wit and made him Marquis of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「卿與朕同源，因事分姓，今可為源氏。

translations.literal: He said: "You and I share one source; because of events the surnames were divided; now you may take the surname Yuan."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "We share one origin; take the surname Yuan."

sentences.zh: 」從擊叛胡白龍，又討吐京胡，皆先登陷陣。

translations.literal: " He followed in striking the rebel Hu Bailong and again campaigned against the Tujing Hu; in both he was first to ascend and break the lines.
translations.idiomatic: He helped crush Bailong and the Tujing Hu, always first over the wall.

sentences.zh: 以功進號平西將軍。

translations.literal: For merit his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he became General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 太武征涼州，以為鄉導，問攻戰之計。

translations.literal: Taiwu campaigned on Liangzhou and used him as native guide, asking plans of attack and battle.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liangzhou campaign Taiwu used him as guide and asked his battle plan.

sentences.zh: 賀曰：「姑臧外有四部鮮卑，各為之援，然皆臣祖父舊人。

translations.literal: He said: "Outside Guzang are four divisions of Xianbei, each a support for it, yet all are my grandfather's old men."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Four Xianbei divisions outside Guzang support the city, but they are my grandfather's old followers."

sentences.zh: 臣願軍前宣國威信，必相率請降。

translations.literal: I wish before the army to proclaim the state's prestige and trust; they will surely lead one another to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Let me proclaim the dynasty's authority—they will surrender in chains.

sentences.zh: 外援既服，然後攻其孤城，拔之如反掌耳。

translations.literal: Once outer support has submitted, then attack its lone city; taking it will be like turning the palm.
translations.idiomatic: Once allies fall away, the lone city will fall at a touch.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 」乃遣賀招慰，下三萬餘落。

translations.literal: " He then sent He to summon and comfort; more than thirty thousand households submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He sent He to win them; thirty thousand households came in.

sentences.zh: 及圍姑臧，由是無外慮，故得專力攻之。

translations.literal: When they besieged Guzang, thereby without outer concern they could concentrate force to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: Besieging Guzang without outside interference, the army could strike with full force.

sentences.zh: 涼州平，以功進爵西平公。

translations.literal: When Liangzhou was pacified, for merit his rank was advanced to Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangzhou fell he was raised to Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 又從征蠕蠕，擊五城吐京胡，討蓋吳諸賊，皆有功，拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He again followed campaigns against the Rouran, struck the Tujing Hu of Wucheng, and campaigned against the bandits of Gai Wu; in all he had merit and was appointed Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: More campaigns against Rouran, Tujing Hu, and Gai Wu won him regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 從駕臨江，為前鋒大將，善撫士卒，加有料敵制勝之謀。

translations.literal: Following the imperial carriage to the river he was Grand General of the Vanguard; he was good at comforting soldiers and moreover had stratagems to gauge the enemy and secure victory.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yangzi he led the vanguard, comforted the troops, and outthought the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賀為人雄果，每遇強寇，輙自奮擊，帝深誡之。

translations.literal: He as a man was bold and resolute; whenever he met strong bandits he would himself spring to attack; the emperor deeply admonished him.
translations.idiomatic: Bold to a fault, he threw himself at every strong foe until the emperor warned him.

sentences.zh: 賀本名破羌，是役也，帝謂曰：「人之立名，宜保其實，何可濫也？

translations.literal: He's original name was Poqiang; in this campaign the emperor said to him: "When a man establishes a name he should preserve its reality—how can it be excessive?"
translations.idiomatic: Born Poqiang, he was told in this war, "A name should fit the deed—yours is too grand."

sentences.zh: 」賜名賀焉。

translations.literal: " He was given the name He.
translations.idiomatic: He was renamed He.

sentences.zh: 拜殿中尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director Within the Hall of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He became director within the hall of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 南安王余為宗愛所殺，賀部勒禁兵，靜遏外內，與南部尚書陸麗決議定策，翼戴文成。

translations.literal: The Prince of Nan'an Yu was killed by Zong Ai; He mustered forbidden troops, quieted and restrained inside and outside, and with Lu Li, Vice Minister of the Southern Masters of Writing, decided the plan and supported and established Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Ai murdered Prince Yu of Nan'an, He rallied the guard, steadied the palace with Lu Li, and enthroned Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 令麗與劉尼馳詣苑中奉迎，賀營中為內應。

translations.literal: He ordered Li and Liu Ni to gallop to the park to welcome him; He in camp was inner responder.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li and Liu Ni to the park to fetch the heir while he held the camp.

sentences.zh: 俄而麗抱文成，單騎而至。

translations.literal: Before long Li embraced Wencheng and came alone on one horse.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li arrived alone on horseback carrying the boy emperor.

sentences.zh: 及即位，賀有力焉。

translations.literal: When he took the throne He had strength in it.
translations.idiomatic: He had done much to place him on the throne.

sentences.zh: 以定策勳，進爵西平王。

translations.literal: For merit in fixing the plan his rank was advanced to Prince of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: For fixing the succession he was made Prince of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 及班賜百寮，敕賀任意取之，辭以江南未賓，漢北不款，府庫不宜致匱。

translations.literal: When rewards were distributed to the hundred officials, an edict ordered He to take as he wished; he declined on the grounds that the south was not yet subject and the north of the Han not yet submissive—the treasury should not be brought to want.
translations.idiomatic: At the general reward he was told to take what he wished but refused, saying the treasury must stay full while north and south were still unconquered.

sentences.zh: 固使取之，唯取戎馬一疋。

translations.literal: They firmly made him take; he took only one horse of the Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed again, he took only one frontier horse.

sentences.zh: 時斷獄多濫。

translations.literal: At the time judging criminal cases was much excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Justice then ran to excess.

sentences.zh: 賀上書曰：「案律，謀反之家，其子孫雖養他族，追還就戮所以絕罪人之類，彰大逆之辜。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "According to the code, in families guilty of rebellion, though descendants were raised in other clans they were pursued back and put to death—this was to cut off the criminal kind and display the guilt of great treason."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote that rebel clans—even children raised elsewhere—were hunted down to extirpate traitors, unlike mere bandits.

sentences.zh: 其為劫賊應誅者，兄弟子侄在遠道隔關津皆不坐。

translations.literal: For those who were robbers deserving execution, brothers, sons, and nephews beyond distant roads and separated by passes and fords were all not implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Yet robbers' kin far beyond the passes were spared—a deliberate distinction.

sentences.zh: 竊惟先朝制律之意，以不同謀，非絕類之罪，故特垂不死之詔。

translations.literal: I reflect that the former court's intent in making the code was that not sharing the plot was not a crime of cutting off the kind, so they specially granted the edict of not dying.
translations.idiomatic: The old code meant non-conspirators were not of the traitor's kind and deserved mercy.

sentences.zh: 若年十三已下，家人首惡，計所不及。

translations.literal: If under thirteen years, the family's chief villain, it was beyond their reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Children under thirteen could not be held to account for the plot.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為可原其命，沒入官。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks their lives may be spared and they be confiscated into government service.
translations.idiomatic: He urged sparing such lives and enrolling them as government slaves.

sentences.zh: 」帝納之。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 出為冀州刺史，改封隴西王。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Jizhou and his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to Jizhou and was made Prince of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 既受除，上書曰：「臣聞人之所寶，莫寶於生命；

translations.literal: Having received the appointment, he memorialized: "Your servant hears that among what men treasure, nothing is treasured like life;
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he wrote: "Of all treasures, life is dearest;

sentences.zh: 德之厚者，莫厚於宥死。

translations.literal: among those thick in virtue, nothing is thicker than sparing death.
translations.idiomatic: among mercies, none greater than sparing the condemned;

sentences.zh: 然犯死之罪，難以盡恕。

translations.literal: Yet crimes deserving death are hard to pardon entirely.
translations.idiomatic: yet capital crimes cannot all be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 權其輕重，有可矜恤。

translations.literal: Weigh their light and heavy; some may be pitied and comforted.
translations.idiomatic: Still, weight and mercy may leave room for pity.

sentences.zh: 今勍寇游魂於北，狡賊負險于南，其在疆場，猶須戍防。

translations.literal: Now fierce bandits wander as souls in the north; crafty foes hold peril in the south; those on the borders still need garrison defense.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce foes haunt north and south; the borders still need men.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為自非大逆、赤手殺人之罪，其坐贓及盜與過誤之愆應入死者，皆可原命，謫守邊境。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks that apart from great treason and bare-handed killing, those whose crimes are embezzlement, theft, and negligent faults that should enter death may all have life spared and be banished to guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Save outright treason and murder, let embezzlers and thieves live as frontier guards.

sentences.zh: 是則已斷之體，更受生成之恩；

translations.literal: Then bodies already cut off would again receive the grace of birth;
translations.idiomatic: Men marked for death would live again;

sentences.zh: 徭役之家，漸蒙休息之惠。

translations.literal: households of corvée would gradually receive the benefit of rest.
translations.idiomatic: corvée households would breathe easier.

sentences.zh: 刑措之化，庶幾在茲。

translations.literal: The transformation of putting away punishments would nearly lie herein.
translations.idiomatic: Thus punishment might nearly disappear.

sentences.zh: 」帝喜納之，已後入死者，皆恕死徙邊。

translations.literal: " The emperor gladly accepted it; afterward those entering death were all spared death and banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor embraced the plan; thereafter capital sentences became exile.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝謂群臣曰：「昔源賀勸朕，宥諸死刑，徙充北籓諸戍。

translations.literal: After a long time the emperor told the ministers: "In the past Yuan He urged me to spare all death penalties and move them to fill the northern frontier garrisons."
translations.idiomatic: Long after, the emperor told his ministers how He had urged sparing the condemned for the northern garrisons.

sentences.zh: 自爾至今，一歲所活，殊為不少。

translations.literal: From then until now, those living a year are quite not few.
translations.idiomatic: Since then the lives saved each year were many.

sentences.zh: 濟命之理既多，邊戍之兵有益。

translations.literal: The principle of saving lives being much, the frontier garrison troops had benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Saving so many lives also strengthened the frontier.

sentences.zh: 苟人人如賀，朕臨天下，復何憂哉！

translations.literal: If every man were like He, I facing all under Heaven—what again would I worry about!
translations.idiomatic: If all my men were like He, what should I fear under heaven!

sentences.zh: 」群臣咸曰：「非忠臣不能進此計，非聖明不能納此言。」

translations.literal: " The ministers all said: "Without a loyal minister one could not advance this plan; without a sage and enlightened ruler one could not accept these words."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers said only a loyal minister proposes such a plan and only a sage accepts it.

sentences.zh: 賀之臨州，鞫獄以情，徭役簡省，清約寬裕，甚得人心。

translations.literal: When He came to the province, he judged cases by sentiment, simplified corvée, was pure, sparing, and broad, and deeply won people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: As governor he judged by the facts, eased corvée, lived sparely, and won deep loyalty.

sentences.zh: 時武邑郡奸人石華告沙門道可與賀謀反，有司以聞。

translations.literal: At the time a villain of Wuyi commandery, Shi Hua, reported the monk Daoke plotting rebellion with He; the offices reported it.
translations.idiomatic: A Wuyi scoundrel accused monk Daoke and He of plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 文成曰：「賀保無此。

translations.literal: Wencheng said: "He assuredly has not this."
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng said, "He would never do that."

sentences.zh: 」乃精加訊檢，華果引誣。

translations.literal: " He then finely added interrogation and examination; Hua indeed led to false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: A careful inquiry proved Hua's frame-up.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使慰勉之。

translations.literal: He then sent an envoy to comfort and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent He words of comfort.

sentences.zh: 帝顧左右曰：「賀忠誠，尚致誣謗，其不若是者，可無慎乎！

translations.literal: The emperor turned to those at his side and said: "He is loyal and sincere—yet he still meets false slander; for those not like this, can one not be cautious!"
translations.idiomatic: He told his attendants, "If even loyal He is slandered, how careful must lesser men be!"

sentences.zh: 」時考殿最，賀政為上第，賜衣馬器物，班宣天下。

translations.literal: " At the time evaluating hall and precinct performance, He's government was top grade; robes, horses, and objects were bestowed and proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the performance review He's province ranked first; rewards were proclaimed empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 後徵拜太尉。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned and appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was later summoned as grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕寇邊，賀從駕討破之。

translations.literal: The Rouran raided the frontier; He followed the imperial carriage and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran raided, He campaigned with the emperor and routed them.

sentences.zh: 及獻文將傳位於京兆王子推，時賀都督諸軍事屯漠南，乃馳傳征賀。

translations.literal: When Xianwen was about to transmit the throne to Zituo, Prince of Jingzhao, at the time He was area commander of all armies garrisoned south of the desert; he then sent a rapid dispatch summoning He.
translations.idiomatic: As Xianwen prepared to abdicate to the Prince of Jingzhao, He was summoned from the desert garrison.

sentences.zh: 賀至，正色固執不可。

translations.literal: When He arrived he sternly and firmly held that it could not be.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived and flatly refused the abdication.

sentences.zh: 即詔持節奉皇帝璽綬以授孝文。

translations.literal: Immediately an edict ordered him to bear the staff and present the imperial seal and cord to Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then had him present the imperial seal to Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 是歲，河西叛，敕遣賀討之，多所降破。

translations.literal: That year Hexi rebelled; an edict sent He to campaign; many submitted and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Hexi rebelled that year, He subdued many by force and surrender.

sentences.zh: 賀依古今兵法及先儒耆舊說，略采至要，為十二陳圖，上之，獻文覽而嘉焉。

translations.literal: He according to ancient and modern military methods and the sayings of former Confucians and elders, briefly selecting the most essential, made twelve formation diagrams and presented them; Xianwen looked and praised them.
translations.idiomatic: He distilled ancient tactics into twelve battle diagrams that Xianwen praised.

sentences.zh: 又都督三道諸軍屯漠南。

translations.literal: He again was area commander of the armies of the three routes garrisoned south of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: He again commanded the three-route army south of the desert.

sentences.zh: 時每歲秋冬，遣軍三道並出，以備北寇，至春中乃班師。

translations.literal: At the time each year autumn and winter the army was sent out in three routes together to prepare against northern raiders; by mid-spring they then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Each autumn three columns marched north; by spring they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賀以勞役京都，又非禦邊長計，乃上言，請募諸州鎮有武勇者三萬人，復其徭賦，厚加振恤，分為三部。

translations.literal: He because it wearied the capital and was also not a long plan for defending the frontier, then submitted, asking to recruit from the garrisons of the provinces thirty thousand men with martial courage, restore their corvée and taxes, richly add relief and support, and divide them into three parts.
translations.idiomatic: He argued the yearly expeditions exhausted the capital and proposed recruiting thirty thousand frontier warriors with tax relief in three divisions.

sentences.zh: 二鎮之間築城，城置萬人，給強弩十二床，武衛三百乘。

translations.literal: Between two garrisons build a fort; in each fort place ten thousand men, supply twelve strong crossbows per bed, three hundred martial guard chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Between two posts he would build forts of ten thousand men with heavy crossbows and war chariots.

sentences.zh: 弩一床給牛六頭，武衛一乘給牛二頭。

translations.literal: Each crossbow bed was supplied six oxen; each martial guard chariot was supplied two oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Each crossbow team took six oxen; each chariot two.

sentences.zh: 多造馬槍及諸器械，使武略大將二人以鎮撫之。

translations.literal: Make many cavalry lances and all instruments; appoint two generals of martial strategy to pacify and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: He would stock lances and gear and station two generals to command them.

sentences.zh: 冬則講武，春則種植，並戍並耕，則兵未勞而有盈蓄矣。

translations.literal: In winter then drill arms; in spring then plant—both garrison and both cultivate—then the army would not be weary and there would be surplus stores.
translations.idiomatic: Winter drill, spring farming—troops would stay fed without annual marches from the capital.

sentences.zh: 又于白道南三處立倉，運近州鎮租粟以充之。

translations.literal: Also south of the White Road at three places establish granaries; transport rent grain from nearby provinces and garrisons to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: He would build three granaries south of the White Road filled with nearby rents.

sentences.zh: 足食足兵，以備不虞，於事為便。

translations.literal: Full food and full troops to prepare against the unforeseen—in affairs it was convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Full granaries and full ranks would guard the frontier cheaply.

sentences.zh: 不可歲常舉眾。

translations.literal: One must not every year always raise the masses.
translations.idiomatic: The realm need not mobilize every year.

sentences.zh: 事寢不報。

translations.literal: The affair was shelved without reply.
translations.idiomatic: The throne filed it without answer.

sentences.zh: 上書稱病乞骸骨，至於再三，乃許之。

translations.literal: He memorialized claiming illness begging for his bones; up to three times; then it was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He begged retirement on illness three times before it was granted.

sentences.zh: 朝有大議，皆就詢訪，又給衣藥珍羞。

translations.literal: When the court had great deliberations all came to inquire of him; he was also given robes, medicine, and delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: Great debates still sought him out; the court sent robes, medicine, and delicacies.

sentences.zh: 太和元年二月，療疾于溫湯。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Taihe he treated illness at the hot springs.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year one, second month, he took the hot springs for his health.

sentences.zh: 孝文、文明太后遣使屢問消息，太醫視疾。

translations.literal: Xiaowen and the Empress Dowager Wenming repeatedly sent envoys to ask after news; the imperial physician attended the illness.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming sent physicians and repeated inquiries.

sentences.zh: 患篤，還于京師。

translations.literal: The illness was grave; he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew worse he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 乃遺令諸子曰：「吾頃以老患辭事，不悟天慈降恩，爵逮於汝。

translations.literal: He then left instructions to his sons, saying: "I recently because of old illness declined affairs, not aware that Heaven's kindness lowered grace, rank reaching you.
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he told his sons, "I quit office with age, never expecting ennoblement to reach you."

sentences.zh: 汝其毋傲吝，毋荒怠，毋奢越，毋嫉妒。

translations.literal: You must not be arrogant and stingy, not be dissolute and negligent, not be extravagant and overstepping, not be jealous.
translations.idiomatic: Be neither arrogant nor stingy, neither slack nor jealous.

sentences.zh: 疑思問，言思審，行思恭，服思度。

translations.literal: In doubt think to ask; in speech think to examine; in conduct think to be respectful; in dress think to measure.
translations.idiomatic: Question what you doubt; weigh your words; honor your conduct; measure your dress.

sentences.zh: 遏惡揚善，親賢遠佞，目觀必真，耳屬必正，忠勤以事君，清約以臨己。

translations.literal: Restrain evil and display good; be close to the worthy and far from flatterers; what the eye sees must be true, what the ear attends must be upright; be loyal and diligent in serving the ruler, pure and sparing in facing yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Repress evil, uplift good, trust the worthy, shun flatterers, see clearly, hear straight, serve loyally, live sparely.

sentences.zh: 吾終之後，所葬，時服單櫝，足申孝心，皞靈明器，一無用也。

translations.literal: After my end, for burial, timely dress in a single coffin is enough to express filial heart; bright spirit bright vessels—none are to be used.
translations.idiomatic: Bury me in plain timely dress in one coffin; no bright spirit goods at all.

sentences.zh: 」三年，薨，贈侍中、太尉、隴西王印綬，諡曰宣王。

translations.literal: " In the third year he died; posthumously awarded Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant, seal and cord of Prince of Longxi; posthumous title Prince Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he died, posthumously palace attendant, grand commandant, and Prince Xuan of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 賜巉輬車及命服、溫明秘器，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: He was given the towering carriage and command robes, warm bright secret vessels, and buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Jinling with imperial funeral gear.

sentences.zh: 長子延，性謹厚，少好學，位侍御中散，賜爵廣武子。

translations.literal: The eldest son Yan, nature careful and thick, in youth loved learning, held the post of Palace Attendant Within the Hall, was enfeoffed Viscount of Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Yan was dutiful and studious, palace attendant within the hall, viscount of Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈涼州刺史，廣武侯，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously awarded Governor of Liangzhou, Marquis of Guangwu, posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He died, posthumously governor of Liangzhou, marquis of Guangwu, posthumous name Jian.

sentences.zh: 子鱗襲。

translations.literal: His son Lin inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lin inherited.

sentences.zh: 延弟思禮，後賜名懷，謙恭寬雅有大度。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Sil, later given the name Huai, was modest, respectful, broad, and elegant and had great measure.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's brother Sil, later Huai, was modest, spacious, and magnanimous.

sentences.zh: 文成末，為侍御中散。

translations.literal: At the end of Wencheng he was Palace Attendant Within the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wencheng he was palace attendant within the hall.

sentences.zh: 父賀辭老，詔受父爵。

translations.literal: His father He declined old age; an edict ordered him to receive his father's rank.
translations.idiomatic: When He retired, an edict let Huai inherit his father's rank.

sentences.zh: 後持節督諸軍屯于漠南，蠕蠕甚憚之。

translations.literal: Later bearing the staff he was area commander of all armies garrisoned south of the desert; the Rouran greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Commanding south of the desert, he made the Rouran fear him.

sentences.zh: 還，除殿中尚書，出為長安鎮將、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On return he was removed as Director Within the Hall and went out as Garrison Commander of Chang'an and Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he directed the masters of writing within the hall, then governed Yong from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 清儉有惠政，善撫恤，劫盜息止。

translations.literal: Pure, sparing, with benevolent government, skilled at comforting and cherishing; banditry ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal and kind, he soothed the people until banditry stopped.

sentences.zh: 復拜殿中尚書，加侍中，參都曹事。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Director Within the Hall, added Palace Attendant, and participated in affairs of All Offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was again director within the hall, palace attendant, and joined all-office affairs.

sentences.zh: 又督諸軍征蠕蠕，六道大將，咸受節度。

translations.literal: He again was area commander of all armies campaigning against the Rouran; six-route grand generals all received his command.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against the Rouran again, six grand generals answered to him.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書令，參議律令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Master of Writing and participated in deliberating codes and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: He became master of writing and helped revise the law.

sentences.zh: 後便降為公。

translations.literal: Later he was then lowered to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 除司州刺史。

translations.literal: He was removed as Governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 又從駕南征，加衛大將軍，領中軍事。

translations.literal: He again followed the imperial carriage on southern campaign and was added General of the Guards and led central military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign he was made guards general in charge of central armies.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職，賜帛三百匹，谷一千石。

translations.literal: He left office on his mother's mourning; silk three hundred bolts and grain one thousand piculs were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: For his mother's mourning he received three hundred bolts of silk and a thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸代，詔使者吊慰。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage visited Dai; an edict ordered envoys to mourn and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Dai, envoys were sent to condole.

sentences.zh: 景明二年，除尚書左僕射，加位特進。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingming he was removed as Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing on the Left and added Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year two he became left vice minister with special advancement.

sentences.zh: 時詔以奸吏犯罪，每多逃遁，肆眚乃出，並皆釋然。

translations.literal: At the time an edict because corrupt officials committing crimes often fled and hid, when the general amnesty was issued they were all released alike.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said corrupt officials who fled would be amnestied like all others.

sentences.zh: 自今犯罪，不問輕重，藏竄者，悉皆遠流。

translations.literal: From now on for crimes, not asking light or heavy, those who hide and flee shall all be banished far.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth all fugitives, whatever the crime, would be exiled.

sentences.zh: 若永避不出，兄弟代徙。

translations.literal: If they forever avoid and do not emerge, brothers shall be moved in their place.
translations.idiomatic: If they never surfaced, their brothers would serve the sentence.

sentences.zh: 懷乃奏曰：「謹案條例，逃吏不在赦限。

translations.literal: Huai then memorialized: "Respectfully examining the regulations, fugitive officials are not within the scope of pardon."
translations.idiomatic: Huai replied that fugitive officials were never within amnesty by regulation.

sentences.zh: 竊惟聖朝之恩，事異前宥，諸流徙在路，尚蒙旋返，況有未發，而仍遣邊戍？

translations.literal: I reflect that the sage court's grace differs from former pardons; all those banished on the road still receive return; how much more those not yet sent out yet still dispatched to frontier garrison?
translations.idiomatic: Exiles already on the road were being recalled—how could fresh fugitives be sent to the frontier?

sentences.zh: 案守宰犯罪，逃走者眾，祿潤既優，尚有茲失，及蒙恩宥，卒然得還。

translations.literal: Examining prefects and magistrates committing crimes, fugitives are many; salary and bounty being superior, they still have such lapses; when they receive gracious pardon they suddenly can return.
translations.idiomatic: Many magistrates fled despite rich salaries, yet would return under grace.

sentences.zh: 今獨苦此等，恐非均一之法。

translations.literal: Now alone to afflict this class—I fear it is not a uniform law.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing only the lowborn, he argued, was not uniform law.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，門下以成式既班，駁奏不許。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted; the Gate and Chamber because the established form had been promulgated, rejected the memorial and did not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the gate; the edict stood and was rejected.

sentences.zh: 懷重奏曰：「臣以為法貴經通，政尚簡要，刑憲之設，所以網羅罪人，苟理之所備，不在繁典。

translations.literal: Huai again memorialized: "Your servant thinks law values passing through, government values simplicity; the setting of penal statutes is to net wrongdoers—if reason is provided for, it is not in a prolix code."
translations.idiomatic: Huai wrote again: law should be simple; nets need not be tangled.

sentences.zh: 伏尋條例，勳品以下，罪發逃亡，遇恩不宥。

translations.literal: Bowing and seeking the regulations, below merit rank, crimes arising and flight, meeting grace are not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Below merit rank, fleeing criminals were denied amnesty.

sentences.zh: 雖欲抑絕奸途，匪為通式。

translations.literal: Though wishing to cut off the wicked path, it is not a passing form.
translations.idiomatic: That rule stifled crime but was no universal pattern.

sentences.zh: 謹按事條，侵官敗法，專據流外，豈九品已上，人皆貞白也？

translations.literal: Respectfully examining the matter regulations—infringing on office and ruining law, solely occupying beyond the current—are all above the ninth rank men all pure and white?
translations.idiomatic: Did only men below the ninth rank sin, while every higher officer was spotless?

sentences.zh: 其諸州守宰，職任清流，至有貪濁，事發逃竄，而遇恩免罪；

translations.literal: The various prefectural governors and magistrates, offices in the pure current, even to greed and defilement, affairs arising and flight and concealment, yet meeting grace are excused from crime;
translations.idiomatic: High prefects who fled corruption were pardoned while merit-rank men alone were hunted;

sentences.zh: 勳品已下，獨求斯例。

translations.literal: below merit rank alone they seek this precedent.
translations.idiomatic: only the humble were denied the same mercy.

sentences.zh: 如此，則寬縱上流，法切於下，育物有差，惠罰不等。

translations.literal: Like this, then leniency is spread on the upper stream while law is sharp on the lower; nurturing things has difference; grace and punishment are not equal.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the mighty were indulged and the low crushed—unequal mercy.

sentences.zh: 又謀逆滔天，經恩尚免，吏犯微罪，獨不蒙赦，使大宥之經不通，開生之路致壅；

translations.literal: Moreover treason floods heaven; passing grace still spares; officials committing slight crimes alone do not receive pardon—making the great pardon's canon not pass, the road of giving life blocked;
translations.idiomatic: Treason itself could be pardoned, yet petty official crimes could not—choking the amnesty itself;

sentences.zh: 進違古典，退乖今律。

translations.literal: advancing it violates ancient canon, retreating it opposes present statutes.
translations.idiomatic: It offended both antiquity and the current code.

sentences.zh: 臣少踐天官，老荷樞要，每見訴訟，出入嗟苦，輒率愚見，以為宜停。

translations.literal: Your servant in youth trod the heavenly offices; in old age bore the pivot's weight; whenever I saw lawsuits, coming and going I sighed in bitterness; I then led my foolish view and thought it should stop.
translations.idiomatic: Long in office, he had watched suits break men and urged the policy be dropped.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，宣武納之。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted; Emperor Xuanwu accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwu accepted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 其年，除車騎大將軍、涼州大中正。

translations.literal: That year he was removed as Grand General of Cavalry and Grand Rectifier of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year he became grand general of cavalry and grand rectifier of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 懷又表曰：「昔世祖升遐，南安在位，出拜東廟為賊臣宗愛所賊。

translations.literal: Huai again memorialized: "In the past when Shizu ascended to the far journey, Nan'an held the throne; going out to pay homage at the eastern temple he was murdered by the traitor minister Zong Ai."
translations.idiomatic: Huai recalled how Emperor Shizu died, Nan'an reigned, and Zong Ai murdered him at the eastern temple.

sentences.zh: 時高宗避難，龍潛苑中，宗愛異圖，神位未立。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Gaozong avoided calamity, dragon hidden in the park; Zong Ai had a different plot; the divine throne was not yet established.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong hid in the park while Zong Ai plotted and the throne stood empty.

sentences.zh: 先臣賀與長孫渴侯、陸麗等奉迎高宗，纂徽寶命。

translations.literal: Your servant's late father He with Zhangsun Kehou, Lu Li, and others welcomed Gaozong and succeeded to the august precious mandate.
translations.idiomatic: His father He with Zhangsun Kehou and Lu Li enthroned Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 麗以扶負聖躬，親所見識，蒙授撫軍、司徒公、平原王。

translations.literal: Li because of supporting and bearing the sacred person, personally witnessed, received appointment as General Who Pacifies the Army, Duke of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li, who carried the emperor in his arms, became general who pacifies the army, master of writing duke, prince of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 興安二年，追論定策之勳，進先臣爵西平王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xing'an, pursuing discussion of merit in fixing the plan, your servant's late father's rank was advanced to Prince of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: In Xing'an year two his father was raised to Prince of Xiping for enthroning the emperor.

sentences.zh: 皇興季年，顯祖將傳大位於京兆王，先臣時都督諸將屯于武川，被征詣京，特見顧問。

translations.literal: In the last year of Huangxing, Emperor Xianzu was about to transmit the great throne to the Prince of Jingzhao; your servant's late father at the time was area commander of all generals garrisoned at Wuchuan, was summoned to the capital, and specially received consultation.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzu would abdicate to Jingzhao, his father was summoned from Wuchuan for counsel.

sentences.zh: 先臣固執不可，顯祖久乃許之，遂命先臣持節授皇帝璽綬于高祖。

translations.literal: Your servant's late father firmly held it could not be; Xianzu after long time then permitted it; he then ordered your servant's late father to bear the staff and present the imperial seal and cord to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: His father refused the abdication until Xianzu yielded, then handed Gaozu the seal.

sentences.zh: 至太和十六年，麗息睿狀秘書，稱其亡父與先臣援立高宗，朝廷追錄，封睿钜鹿郡開國公。

translations.literal: By the sixteenth year of Taihe, Li's son Rui reported to the secretariat, saying his dead father with your servant's late father supported and established Gaozong; the court pursued the record and enfeoffed Rui Duke of Julu commandery, state-founder.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe sixteen Rui won a Julu founding dukedom by citing his father's role with He's in enthroning Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 臣時丁艱草土，不容及例。

translations.literal: Your servant at the time was in grass-soil mourning and could not reach the precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Huai was in mourning and could not claim then.

sentences.zh: 至二十年，除臣雍州刺史。

translations.literal: By the twentieth year your servant was removed as Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty he became governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 臨發奉辭，面奏先帝，申先臣舊勳。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure paying farewell, he faced the late emperor and memorialized his late father's old merit.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving for Yong, he reminded the late emperor of his father's service.

sentences.zh: 時蒙敕旨，但赴所臨，尋當別判。

translations.literal: At the time he received an edict: only go to what you oversee; soon there will be separate judgment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict told him to take the post; reward would follow.

sentences.zh: 至二十一年，車駕幸雍，臣復陳聞。

translations.literal: By the twenty-first year the imperial carriage visited Yong; your servant again stated it.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-one, when the emperor visited Yong, he spoke again.

sentences.zh: 時蒙敕旨，征還當授。

translations.literal: At the time he received an edict: on recall he would be awarded.
translations.idiomatic: He was told he would be enfeoffed on recall.

sentences.zh: 自宮車晏駕，遂爾不申。

translations.literal: From the imperial carriage's peaceful departure it was thus not stated.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's death he could not press it.

sentences.zh: 竊惟先臣，遠則授立高宗，寶曆不墜；

translations.literal: I reflect on your servant's late father—far then he received and established Gaozong; the precious succession did not fall;
translations.idiomatic: His father had far back saved the succession when Gaozong was made emperor;

sentences.zh: 近則陳力顯祖，神器有歸。

translations.literal: near then he offered strength to Xianzu; the sacred vessel had a return.
translations.idiomatic: near at hand he secured Xianzu's abdication to Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 如斯之勳，超世之事也。

translations.literal: Merit like this is a matter surpassing the age.
translations.idiomatic: Such merit outshone his generation.

sentences.zh: 麗以父功，而獲山河之賞；

translations.literal: Li by his father's merit obtained reward of mountains and rivers;
translations.idiomatic: Li won mountains-and-rivers reward for his father's deed;

sentences.zh: 臣有家勳，不沾茅土之錫。

translations.literal: your servant has family merit yet does not touch the grant of thatch and soil.
translations.idiomatic: Huai's house had equal merit yet no fief.

sentences.zh: 得否相懸，請垂裁處。

translations.literal: Gain and denial hang apart—I ask to let judgment fall.
translations.idiomatic: The disparity was unjust—he asked the throne to decide.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「宿老元臣，雲如所訴，訪之史官，頗亦言此。

translations.literal: " The edict said: "The old veteran minister of long standing—as the clouds report, inquiring of the historiographers it is quite also spoken thus."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said the histories confirmed his plea.

sentences.zh: 可依授北馮翊郡開國公，食邑九百戶。」

translations.literal: He may be enfeoffed according to appointment as Duke of Beifengyi commandery, state-founder, fief of nine hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: He was made founding duke of Beifengyi with nine hundred households.

sentences.zh: 又詔為使持節，加侍中、行台，巡行北邊六鎮，恆、北、朔三州，賑給貧乏，兼采風謠，考論殿最，事之得失，先決後聞。

translations.literal: He was again edicted Bearer of the Staff, added Palace Attendant and Mobile Headquarters, touring the northern frontier six garrisons and the three provinces Heng, Bei, and Shuo, relieving the poor and needy, also gathering folk songs, evaluating hall and precinct performance, the gains and losses of affairs—decide first then report.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent with a staff as mobile headquarters to tour six northern garrisons and three provinces, aid the poor, hear folk songs, and judge officials.

sentences.zh: 自京師遷洛，邊朔遙遠，加以連年旱儉，百姓困弊。

translations.literal: From the capital's move to Luoyang the northern frontier was far; moreover successive years of drought and dearth—the hundred surnames were distressed and worn.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to Luoyang the north starved through drought after drought.

sentences.zh: 懷銜命撫導，存恤有方，便宜運轉，有無通濟。

translations.literal: Huai received the mandate to guide and comfort; preserving and cherishing had method; convenient transport and transfer—having and not having mutually aided.
translations.idiomatic: Huai fed the frontier wisely and kept supplies moving.

sentences.zh: 時後父于勁勢傾朝野，勁兄子祚與懷宿昔通婚，時為沃野鎮將，頗有受納。

translations.literal: At the time the empress's father Yu Jin's power tilted court and countryside; Jin's elder brother's son Zuo had with Huai an old marriage; at the time he was Garrison Commander of Woye and quite had accepting and taking.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yu Jin's kin ruled the court; his nephew Zuo, Huai's in-law and Woye commander, took bribes.

sentences.zh: 將入鎮，祚郊迎道左，懷不與相聞，即劾祚免官。

translations.literal: About to enter the garrison, Zuo met him on the road to the left in the suburbs; Huai did not communicate with him and immediately impeached Zuo and removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo met him outside town; Huai ignored him and impeached him from office.

sentences.zh: 懷朔鎮將元尼須與懷少舊，亦貪穢狼籍。

translations.literal: The Garrison Commander of Huaishuo Yuan Nixu had with Huai an old youth acquaintance and also was greedy and defiled in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishuo commander Yuan Nixu, an old friend, was likewise corrupt.

sentences.zh: 置酒請懷，曰：「命之長短，由卿之口，豈可不相寬貸？

translations.literal: He set out wine and invited Huai, saying: "Whether life is long or short is by your mouth—how can you not mutually grant leniency?"
translations.idiomatic: Nixu wined him and said, "My life is in your mouth—won't you spare me?"

sentences.zh: 」懷曰：「今日之集，乃是源懷與故人飲酒之坐，非鞫獄之所也。

translations.literal: " Huai said: "Today's gathering is Yuan Huai drinking wine with an old friend—it is not a place for judging cases."
translations.idiomatic: Huai said, "Tonight I drink with a friend—not a court of justice."

sentences.zh: 明日公庭，始為使人檢鎮將罪狀之處。

translations.literal: Tomorrow in the public court is where I begin as envoy to inspect garrison commanders' crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow at court I start inspecting the garrison commanders' crimes.

sentences.zh: 」尼須揮淚而已，無以對之。

translations.literal: Ni Xu could only shed tears and had nothing to say.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Xu wept and could not answer.

sentences.zh: 既而懷錶劾尼須。

translations.literal: Before long Huai memorialized against Ni Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Huai impeached Ni Xu.

sentences.zh: 其奉公不撓，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His serving the public without bending—all were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the public without yielding—always like this.

sentences.zh: 時百姓為豪強陵壓，積年枉滯，一朝見申者，日有百數。

translations.literal: At the time the common people were oppressed by powerful families; cases unjustly held up for years—in a single morning those vindicated numbered in the hundreds daily.
translations.idiomatic: People crushed by great houses had cases stalled for years; in one morning hundreds were cleared daily.

sentences.zh: 所上事宜，便於北邊者，凡三十餘條，皆見嘉納。

translations.literal: Matters he submitted that would benefit the northern frontier numbered more than thirty articles, all accepted with praise.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty proposals useful to the north were all praised and adopted.

sentences.zh: 正始元年九月，有告蠕蠕率十二萬騎，六道並進，欲直趣沃野、懷朔，南寇恆、代。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Zhengshi, someone reported the Rouran leading 120,000 horsemen on six routes together, aiming straight for Woye and Huaishuo and south to raid Heng and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Zhengshi 1, word came that the Rouran had 120,000 horse on six roads toward Woye and Huaishuo and south against Heng and Dai.

sentences.zh: 詔懷以本官加使持節、侍中，出據北蕃。

translations.literal: Huai was ordered with his original office plus Staff with credentials and Palace Attendant to go out and hold the northern marches.
translations.idiomatic: Huai kept his rank, gained staff credentials and Palace Attendant, and went to hold the northern border.

sentences.zh: 指授規略，隨須徵發，諸所處分，皆以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Strategy was set for him; troops were raised as needed; all dispositions were by expedient authority.
translations.idiomatic: He was given strategy, could levy as needed, and act on expedient authority.

sentences.zh: 又詔懷子直寢徵隨懷北行。

translations.literal: Also ordered Huai's son Zhizhen summoned to follow Huai north.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhizhen was summoned to go north with him.

sentences.zh: 詔賜馬一匹、細鎧一具、禦槊一枚。

translations.literal: He was granted one horse, one set of fine armor, and one imperial lance.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave him a horse, fine armor, and an imperial lance.

sentences.zh: 懷拜受既訖，乃於其庭，跨鞍執槊，躍馬大呼。

translations.literal: When Huai had finished bowing in acceptance, in his courtyard he mounted, grasped the lance, spurred the horse, and shouted loudly.
translations.idiomatic: After the bow he mounted in his courtyard, seized the lance, spurred his horse, and shouted.

sentences.zh: 顧謂賓客曰：「氣力雖衰，尚得如此。

translations.literal: Turning to his guests he said: "Though my strength has waned, I can still do this.
translations.idiomatic: He told his guests, "Weak as I am, I can still do this.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕雖畏壯輕老，我亦未便可欺。

translations.literal: The Rouran may fear the strong and slight the old, but I am not so easily fooled.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran fear the strong and mock the old—but I am not so easily fooled.

sentences.zh: 今奉廟勝之規，總驍捍之眾，足以擒其酋帥，獻俘闕下耳。

translations.literal: Now following the temple's victorious plan and commanding fierce troops, it is enough to seize their chiefs and present captives below the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Under the court's winning plan, with fierce troops, I can still take their chiefs and bring captives to the palace."

sentences.zh: 」時年六十一。

translations.literal: He was then sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 懷至雲中，蠕蠕亡遁。

translations.literal: When Huai reached Yunzhong, the Rouran fled and vanished.
translations.idiomatic: At Yunzhong the Rouran fled.

sentences.zh: 旋至恆、代，乃案視諸鎮左右要害之地，可以築城置戍之處，皆量其高下，揣其厚薄，及儲糧積仗之宜，犬牙相救之勢，凡表五十八條，宣武並從之。

translations.literal: Soon he reached Heng and Dai, then inspected all posts along the garrisons for places where walls and garrisons might be built; he measured heights, gauged thickness, grain stores and arms, and interlocking relief—in all fifty-eight memorial articles, all accepted by Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: At Heng and Dai he surveyed garrison terrain for walls and posts, heights, thickness, grain, arms, and mutual relief—fifty-eight memorials, all accepted by Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司徒公，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously made Duke of Situ, posthumous name Hui (Kind).
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Duke of Situ, posthumous name Kind.

sentences.zh: 懷性寬簡，不好煩碎。

translations.literal: Huai was broad and simple by nature and disliked petty detail.
translations.idiomatic: Huai was easygoing and hated petty detail.

sentences.zh: 恆語人曰：「為政貴當舉綱，何必須太子細也！

translations.literal: He often told people: "In governing, what matters is to raise the main rope—why must one be as fine as a crown prince's threads!
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Government needs the main rope raised—why fuss like crown-prince threadwork!

sentences.zh: 如為屋，但外望高顯，楹棟平正，足矣。

translations.literal: It is like building a house: only that the outside looks high and bright and pillars and beams are level is enough.
translations.idiomatic: A house needs only a lofty front and level beams.

sentences.zh: 斧斤不平，非屋病也。

translations.literal: If axe and adze work is uneven, that is not the house's sickness."
translations.idiomatic: Uneven carpentry is not the house's fault."

sentences.zh: 」性不飲酒，而喜以飲人。

translations.literal: By nature he did not drink, yet he delighted in treating others to drink.
translations.idiomatic: He did not drink but loved treating others.

sentences.zh: 好接賓客，雅善音律，雖在白首，至宴居之暇，常自操絲竹。

translations.literal: He loved receiving guests and was skilled in music; though white-haired, in leisure at banquets he often played string and bamboo himself.
translations.idiomatic: He loved guests and music; though white-haired, at leisure he often played strings himself.

sentences.zh: 子子邕，字靈和。

translations.literal: Son Ziyong, styled Linghe.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziyong, styled Linghe.

sentences.zh: 少好文雅，篤志於學，推誠待士，士多歸之。

translations.literal: From youth he loved letters and was earnest in study; he treated scholars with sincerity and many gathered to him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved letters, studied hard, and won scholars by sincerity.

sentences.zh: 累遷夏州刺史。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Governor of Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Governor of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 時沃野鎮人破六韓拔陵首為反亂，統萬逆徒，寇害應接。

translations.literal: At the time people of Woye Garrison took Poliuhan Baling as first to raise rebellion; rebels of Tongwan pressed in with ceaseless raids.
translations.idiomatic: When Woye men followed Poliuhan Baling in the first northern revolt, Tongwan rebels harried without pause.

sentences.zh: 子邕嬰城自守，城中糧盡，煮馬皮而食之。

translations.literal: Ziyong closed the city and held it; grain in the city ran out and they boiled horse hides to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong held the city; grain ran out and they boiled horsehide.

sentences.zh: 子邕善綏撫，無有離貳。

translations.literal: Ziyong was good at soothing and there was no defection.
translations.idiomatic: He soothed the people and none deserted.

sentences.zh: 以饑饉轉切，欲自出求糧，留子延伯據守。

translations.literal: As famine grew acute he wished to go out himself to seek grain and leave Yanbo to hold the defense.
translations.idiomatic: Famine sharpened; he would seek grain himself and leave Yanbo to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 僚屬僉雲，未若棄城俱去，更展規略。

translations.literal: His staff all said it would be better to abandon the city and leave together and plan anew.
translations.idiomatic: His staff urged abandoning the city and regrouping.

sentences.zh: 子邕泣請於眾曰：「吾世荷國恩，此是吾死地，更欲何求！

translations.literal: Ziyong wept and begged the crowd: "Our house has received the state's grace for generations; this is my place to die—what more do I seek!"
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, he told them, "My house owes the state for generations; this is where I die—what more could I want!"

sentences.zh: 」遂自率羸弱向東夏運糧。

translations.literal: He then led the weak himself east to Xia to transport grain.
translations.idiomatic: He led the weak east to Xia to bring grain.

sentences.zh: 延伯與將士送出城，哭而拜辭，三軍莫不嗚咽。

translations.literal: Yanbo and the troops escorted him from the city; they wept and bowed in farewell and the whole army sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo and the troops saw him out, weeping and bowing; the army sobbed.

sentences.zh: 子邕為朔方胡帥曹阿各拔所邀，力屈被執。

translations.literal: Ziyong was waylaid by the Shuo barbarian chief Cao A Geba and, strength spent, was seized.
translations.idiomatic: The Shuo chief Cao A Geba intercepted him; spent, he was taken.

sentences.zh: 乃密遣人齎書間行與城中云：「大軍在近，汝其奉忠，勿移其操。

translations.literal: He secretly sent a man with a letter by hidden route to the city saying: "The great army is near—hold loyalty and do not change your resolve."
translations.idiomatic: He sent a secret letter: "The army is near—stay loyal and do not waver."

sentences.zh: 」子邕雖被囚束，雅為胡人所敬，常以百姓禮事之。

translations.literal: Though Ziyong was bound, the barbarians respected him and always treated him with the courtesy due the people.
translations.idiomatic: Though captive, the barbarians respected him and treated him with civil courtesy.

sentences.zh: 子邕為陳安危禍福之端，勸阿各拔令降。

translations.literal: Ziyong set forth the roots of safety and danger, fortune and misfortune, and urged A Geba to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He explained safety and danger and urged A Geba to surrender.

sentences.zh: 將從之，未果而死。

translations.literal: Just as A Geba was about to follow, he died before it was done.
translations.idiomatic: A Geba was about to yield when Ziyong died.

sentences.zh: 拔弟桑生代總部眾，竟隨子邕降。

translations.literal: A Geba's younger brother Sang Sheng succeeded in command of the tribe and in the end followed Ziyong in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Sang Sheng took the tribe and finally submitted as Ziyong had urged.

sentences.zh: 時北海王顥為大行台，子邕具陳諸賊可滅狀。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao was Grand Commissioner; Ziyong fully set forth how the rebels could be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao was Grand Commissioner; Ziyong laid out how to destroy the rebels.

sentences.zh: 顥給子邕兵，令其先出。

translations.literal: Hao gave Ziyong troops and ordered him to advance first.
translations.idiomatic: Hao gave him troops and sent him ahead.

sentences.zh: 時東夏合境反叛，所在屯結。

translations.literal: At the time the whole of eastern Xia rebelled and bands gathered everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: All eastern Xia rose; bands formed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 子邕轉戰而前，九旬之中，凡數十戰，乃平東夏。

translations.literal: Ziyong fought forward; in ninety days he fought several dozen battles and then pacified eastern Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He fought on; in ninety days and dozens of battles he pacified eastern Xia.

sentences.zh: 徵稅租粟，運糧統萬，於是二夏漸寧。

translations.literal: He levied grain tax and transported grain to Tongwan, and the two Xia regions gradually grew calm.
translations.idiomatic: He levied grain, shipped it to Tongwan, and both Xia lands grew quiet.

sentences.zh: 及蕭寶夤等為賊所敗，關右騷擾，時子邕新平黑城，遂率士馬並夏州募義人，鼓行南出。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin and others were defeated by rebels and Guanxi was in turmoil, Ziyong had just pacified Heicheng and led troops and horses with Xiazhou volunteers south in martial array.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin and others fell in Guanxi, Ziyong, fresh from Heicheng, marched south with Xiazhou volunteers.

sentences.zh: 賊帥康維摩守鋸穀，斷絕<嬰瓦>棠橋。

translations.literal: The rebel chief Kang Weimo held Juguli and cut the Yingtang Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel Kang Weimo held Juguli and cut Yingtang Bridge.

sentences.zh: 子邕與戰，大破之，禽維摩。

translations.literal: Ziyong fought him, routed him greatly, and captured Weimo.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong routed him and took Weimo.

sentences.zh: 又攻破賊帥契官斤于楊氏堡。

translations.literal: He also defeated the rebel chief Qiguan Jin at Yangshi Fort.
translations.idiomatic: He also beat Qiguan Jin at Yangshi Fort.

sentences.zh: 出自西夏，至於東夏，轉戰千里。

translations.literal: From western Xia to eastern Xia he fought a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: From western to eastern Xia he fought a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 至是，朝廷始得委問。
