translations.literal: Only then did the court begin to send formal inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the court send formal inquiries.

sentences.zh: 除兼行台尚書。

translations.literal: He was made Concurrent Mobile Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was made concurrent Mobile Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 復破賊帥紇單步胡提于曲沃，明帝璽書勞勉之。

translations.literal: He again defeated the rebel chief Hedan Buhuti at Quwo; Emperor Ming sent an imperial letter to praise and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: He beat Hedan Buhuti at Quwo; Ming sent an imperial letter of praise.

sentences.zh: 子邕在白水郡破賊率宿勤明達子阿非軍，多所斬獲。

translations.literal: At Baishui commandery Ziyong defeated the rebel force of Suqin Mingda's son Afei and beheaded and captured many.
translations.idiomatic: At Baishui he routed Afei, son of Suqin Mingda, and took many heads.

sentences.zh: 除給事黃門侍郎，封樂平縣公。

translations.literal: He was made Attendant of the Yellow Gate and enfeoffed Duke of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: He was Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Duke of Leping.

sentences.zh: 以葛榮久逼信都，詔子邕為北討都督。

translations.literal: Because Ge Rong long pressed Xindu, Ziyong was ordered Northern Campaign Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong long besieged Xindu; Ziyong was made Northern Campaign Commander.

sentences.zh: 時相州刺史、安樂王鑒據鄴反，敕子邕與都督李神軌先討平之。

translations.literal: At the time Xiangzhou Inspector, Prince of Anle Yuan Jian, held Ye in rebellion; an edict ordered Ziyong and Commissioner Li Shengui to pacify him first.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Anle Yuan Jian held Ye; Ziyong and Li Shengui were ordered to crush him first.

sentences.zh: 改封陽平縣公。

translations.literal: His fief was changed to Duke of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: His fief became Duke of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 遂與裴衍發鄴，討葛榮。

translations.literal: He then with Pei Yan marched from Ye against Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He then left Ye with Pei Yan against Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 而信都城陷，除子邕冀州刺史，與裴衍俱進。

translations.literal: But Xindu city fell; Ziyong was made Jizhou Inspector and advanced with Pei Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Xindu fell; he was made Jizhou Inspector and advanced with Pei Yan.

sentences.zh: 子邕戰敗而歿，贈司空，諡曰莊穆。

translations.literal: Ziyong was defeated in battle and died; posthumously Minister of Works, posthumous name Zhuangmu (Solemn and Reverent).
translations.idiomatic: He was beaten and died; posthumously Minister of Works, posthumous name Solemn.

sentences.zh: 子邕弟子恭，字靈順，聰敏好學。

translations.literal: Ziyong's younger brother's son Zigong, styled Lingshun, was clever, fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Zigong, styled Lingshun, was clever and studious.

sentences.zh: 稍遷尚書北主客郎，攝南主客事。

translations.literal: He rose gradually to Northern Host-guest Gentleman in the Masters of Writing and concurrently handled southern host-guest affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Northern Host-guest Gentleman and handled southern host-guest affairs too.

sentences.zh: 時梁亡人許周自雲梁給事黃門侍郎，朝士咸共信待。

translations.literal: At the time Xu Zhou, a refugee from Liang, claimed to be Liang Attendant of the Yellow Gate; court scholars all trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang refugee Xu Zhou claimed to be Liang Yellow Gate Attendant; the court trusted him.

sentences.zh: 子恭奏以為真偽難辨，請下徐、楊二州密訪。

translations.literal: Zigong memorialized that true and false were hard to tell and asked that Xu and Yang provinces be secretly investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong said the claim was doubtful and asked secret inquiry in Xu and Yang.

sentences.zh: 周果以罪歸闕，詐假職位，如子恭所疑。

translations.literal: Zhou indeed returned to the capital under charge, having falsely claimed office, just as Zigong had suspected.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was brought back under charge for false rank, as Zigong had said.

sentences.zh: 河州羌卻鐵匆反，詔子恭為行台討之。

translations.literal: Qie Tiecang of Hezhou Qiang rebelled; Zigong was ordered Mobile Commissioner to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhou Qiang Qie Tiecang rebelled; Zigong was sent to attack.

sentences.zh: 子恭示以威恩，兩旬間悉降。

translations.literal: Zigong showed both sternness and kindness; within twenty days all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He mixed sternness and grace; in twenty days all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: The court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised him.

sentences.zh: 正光元年，為行台左丞，巡北邊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengguang he was Mobile Secretariat Left Director, touring the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengguang 1 he toured the north as Mobile Left Director.

sentences.zh: 轉為起部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Bureau Director of Construction.
translations.idiomatic: He became Bureau Director of Construction.

sentences.zh: 明堂、辟雍並未建就，子恭上書，求加經綜。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall and Imperial Academy were not yet finished; Zigong submitted a memorial asking to oversee them further.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Hall and Imperial Academy were unfinished; Zigong asked to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 書奏，從之。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted.

sentences.zh: 稍遷豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He rose gradually to Yuzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Yuzhou Inspector.

sentences.zh: 頻以軍功，加鎮南將軍，兼尚書行台。

translations.literal: Repeatedly for military merit he was made General Who Pacifies the South and Concurrent Mobile Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: For repeated merit he was General Who Pacifies the South and concurrent Mobile Director.

sentences.zh: 元顥之入洛也，加子恭車騎將軍；

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Zigong was made General of Cavalry and Chariots;
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao took Luoyang, Zigong was made General of Cavalry and Chariots;

sentences.zh: 子恭不敢拒之，而頻遣間使參莊帝動靜。

translations.literal: Zigong did not dare refuse him but repeatedly sent secret envoys to report Emperor Zhuang's movements.
translations.idiomatic: he did not dare refuse but sent secret reports on Emperor Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，顥敗，車駕還洛，錄前後征討功，封臨潁縣侯，侍中。

translations.literal: Before long Hao was defeated, the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang, and for past campaign merit Zigong was enfeoffed Marquis of Linying, Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hao fell, the emperor returned, and Zigong was Marquis of Linying and Palace Attendant for past merit.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮之死也，世隆、度律斷據河橋，詔子恭為都督以討之。

translations.literal: At Erzhu Rong's death, Shilong and Dulü held the He Bridge; Zigong was ordered commander to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died, Shilong and Dulü held He Bridge; Zigong was ordered to attack.

sentences.zh: 尋而太府卿李苗夜燒河橋，世隆退走，以子恭兼尚書僕射，為大行台、大都督。

translations.literal: Soon Grand Steward Li Miao burned the He Bridge by night; Shilong retreated and Zigong was made Concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Commissioner, and Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Li Miao burned He Bridge by night; Shilong fled; Zigong became Vice Director, Grand Commissioner, and Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝初，以預定策勳，封臨汝縣子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Jiemin he was enfeoffed Viscount of Linru for merit in fixing the succession.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiemin's accession he was Viscount of Linru for fixing the succession.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，入為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he entered as Minister of Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi he became Minister of Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 以子恭前在豫州戰功，追賞襄城縣男。

translations.literal: For Zigong's earlier merit at Yuzhou he was retroactively enfeoffed Baron of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: For Yuzhou merit he was retroactively Baron of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 又論子恭余效，封新城縣子。

translations.literal: Again for Zigong's remaining achievements he was enfeoffed Viscount of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Further merit made him Viscount of Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 子恭尋表請轉授第五子文盛，許之。

translations.literal: Zigong soon memorialized asking to transfer the rank to his fifth son Wensheng; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to give the rank to his fifth son Wensheng and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 天平初，除中書監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping he was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianping's start he was Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜魏尹，又為齊神武王軍司。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made Wei Governor and also Military Adviser to Prince Qi Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he was Wei Governor and adviser to Prince Qi Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空公，諡曰文獻。

translations.literal: At death posthumously Duke of Works, posthumous name Wenxian (Cultured and Manifest).
translations.idiomatic: He died posthumously Duke of Works, posthumous name Cultured.

sentences.zh: 子彪。

translations.literal: Son Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Son Biao.

sentences.zh: 彪字文宗，學涉機警，少有名譽。

translations.literal: Biao, styled Wenzong, was learned, quick-witted, and from youth had a name for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Biao, styled Wenzong, was learned and quick; from youth he was known.

sentences.zh: 魏永安中，以父功賜爵臨潁縣伯。

translations.literal: In Wei's Yongan era, for his father's merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Linying.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongan, for his father's merit, he was Baron of Linying.

sentences.zh: 天平四年，為涼州大中正。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianping he was Liangzhou Grand Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: Tianping 4 he was Liangzhou Grand Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 及齊文襄攝選，沙汰台郎，以文宗為尚書祠部郎中。

translations.literal: When Prince Qi Wenxiang took charge of selection, he purged Secretariat gentlemen and made Wenzong Director of the Ancestral Temples Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiang purged Secretariat gentlemen, Wenzong became Director of the Ancestral Temples Bureau.

sentences.zh: 皇建二年，累遷涇州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangjian he rose in succession to Jingzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Huangjian 2 he rose to Jingzhou Inspector.

sentences.zh: 文宗以恩信待物，甚得邊境之和，為鄰人所欽服，前政被抄掠者，多被放遣。

translations.literal: Wenzong treated men with kindness and trust and won great harmony on the frontier; neighboring peoples admired and submitted, and many earlier seized in raids were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled the border by kindness and trust; neighbors submitted and returned many earlier captives.

sentences.zh: 累遷秦州刺史，乘傳之府，特給後部鼓吹。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Qinzhou Inspector; riding post-haste to his prefecture he was specially granted rear guard music.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Qinzhou Inspector and was given rear guard music on post horses.

sentences.zh: 時李貞聘陳，陳主云：「齊朝還遣源涇州來在瓜步，真可謂通和矣。

translations.literal: At the time Li Zhen was envoy to Chen; the Chen ruler said: "Our court has again sent Source of the Jingzhou at Guabu—truly we are in communication."
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhen went to Chen, the Chen ruler said, "Qi has again sent the man from Jingzhou to Guabu—how open we are."

sentences.zh: 」武平三年，授秘書監。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wuping he was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wuping 3 he was Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 陳將吳明徹寇淮南，曆陽、瓜步相尋失守。

translations.literal: The Chen general Wu Mingche attacked Huainan; Liyang and Guabu fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Chen general Wu Mingche took Huainan; Liyang and Guabu fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 趙彥深於起居省密訪文宗討捍之計。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshen at the Palace Secretariat secretly consulted Wenzong on plans to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshen secretly asked Wenzong at the Secretariat how to resist.

sentences.zh: 文宗曰：「國家待遇淮南，失之同於蒿箭。

translations.literal: Wenzong said: "The state's treatment of Huainan has lost it as easily as an arrow in the weeds."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong said, "We treat Huainan like an arrow lost in weeds."

sentences.zh: 以為宜以淮南委之王琳。

translations.literal: He thought Huainan ought to be entrusted to Wang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: He thought Huainan should go to Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 琳於曇頊，不肯北面事之明矣。

translations.literal: Lin at Tanling plainly would not bow north to Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Lin at Tanling would never bow north to Chen Ming.

sentences.zh: 」彥深曰：「弟此良圖。

translations.literal: Yanshen said: "Brother, this is a fine plan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen said, "A fine plan, brother.

sentences.zh: 但以口舌爭來十日，已是不見從。

translations.literal: But to argue with words for ten days already went unheard.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days of talk already failed.

sentences.zh: 時事如此，安可盡言！

translations.literal: Affairs are as they are—how can one speak everything!"
translations.idiomatic: Things are as they are—how can one say it all!"

sentences.zh: 」因相顧流涕。

translations.literal: They then looked at each other and wept.
translations.idiomatic: They wept together.

sentences.zh: 及齊平，與陽休之等十八人入京，授儀同大將軍、司成下大夫。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, with Yang Xiuzhi and eighteen others he entered the capital and was made General of the Fourth Rank, Grand Master of the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he entered the capital with Yang Xiuzhi and eighteen others as Fourth-rank General and Academy Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，拜莒州刺史。

translations.literal: In Sui's Kaihuang era he was made Juzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang he was Juzhou Inspector.

sentences.zh: 遇病去官，卒。

translations.literal: He fell ill, left office, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced retirement; he died.

sentences.zh: 文宗以貴族子弟升朝列，才識敏贍，以幹局見知。

translations.literal: Wenzong as a nobleman's son rose in the court ranks; his talent and judgment were quick and he was known for practical capacity.
translations.idiomatic: A noble's son, he rose fast; quick and capable, he was known for getting things done.

sentences.zh: 然好遊貴要之門，時論以為善附會。

translations.literal: Yet he loved visiting the houses of the great; opinion held he was good at currying favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he courted the powerful; opinion said he knew how to flatter.

sentences.zh: 子師，字踐言。

translations.literal: Son Shi, styled Jianyan.
translations.idiomatic: Son Shi, styled Jianyan.

sentences.zh: 少知名，明辯有識悟，尤以吏事自許。

translations.literal: From youth he was known; sharp in debate and with insight, he especially prided himself on clerical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Known from youth, sharp and insightful, he especially trusted his skill in office work.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為尚書左外兵郎中，又攝祠部。

translations.literal: In Qi he was Left Outer Military Gentleman and also handled the Ancestral Temples Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi he was Left Outer Military Gentleman and handled the temples bureau.

sentences.zh: 後屬孟夏，以龍見請雩。

translations.literal: Later in midsummer, because the Dragon Star appeared, rain sacrifice was requested.
translations.idiomatic: In midsummer the Dragon Star appeared and rain sacrifice was requested.

sentences.zh: 時高阿那肱為錄尚書事，謂為真龍出見，大驚喜。

translations.literal: At the time Gao Anagong was Recorder of the Masters of Writing and said a true dragon had appeared, greatly delighted.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Anagong, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, said a real dragon had appeared and rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 問龍所在，云：「作何顏色？

translations.literal: He asked where the dragon was and what color it was.
translations.idiomatic: He asked where it was and what color.

sentences.zh: 」師整容云：「此是龍星初見，依禮當雩祭郊壇，非謂真龍別有所降。

translations.literal: Shi composed himself and said: "This is the Dragon Star's first appearance; by rite rain sacrifice is at the suburban altar—it does not mean a true dragon has descended elsewhere."
translations.idiomatic: Shi said calmly, "This is the Dragon Star's first sighting; rite calls for suburban rain sacrifice—not a dragon descending elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 」阿那肱忿然作色曰：「漢兒多事，強知星宿！

translations.literal: Anagong flushed angrily and said: "Han fellows meddle too much, pretending to know the stars!"
translations.idiomatic: Anagong snapped, "Han meddlers, pretending to know the stars!"

sentences.zh: 」祭事不行。

translations.literal: The sacrifice was not performed.
translations.idiomatic: The rite was dropped.

sentences.zh: 師出，竊歎曰：「國家大事，在祀與戎，禮既廢也，其能久乎？

translations.literal: Shi left and sighed in private: "The state's great affairs lie in sacrifice and arms; when rites are abandoned, can it last long?
translations.idiomatic: Leaving, he sighed, "Sacrifice and arms are the state's root; rites abandoned—how long can it last?

sentences.zh: 齊亡無日矣！

translations.literal: Qi's fall is not far!"
translations.idiomatic: Qi has no days left!"

sentences.zh: 」尋周武帝平齊，授司賦上士。

translations.literal: Soon Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi and made him Superior Tax Master.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhou Wu pacified Qi and made him Superior Tax Master.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，累遷尚書左丞，以明幹著稱。

translations.literal: When Sui Wendi received the mandate he rose in succession to Left Assistant Minister of the Masters of Writing and was famed for clarity and efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: When Wendi took the throne he rose to Left Assistant Minister, famed for clarity and drive.

sentences.zh: 時蜀王秀頗違法度，乃以師為益州總管司馬。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Shu Xiu often violated law; Shi was made Staff Major to the Yizhou Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shu Xiu broke the law; Shi was made Yizhou staff major.

sentences.zh: 俄而秀被征，秀恐京師有變，將謝病。

translations.literal: Before long Xiu was summoned; fearing trouble in the capital, he meant to plead illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xiu was summoned; fearing the capital, he would plead illness.

sentences.zh: 師數勸之，不可違命。

translations.literal: Shi repeatedly urged him that he could not defy the command.
translations.idiomatic: Shi urged him not to defy the order.

sentences.zh: 秀乃作色曰：「此我家事，何預卿也？

translations.literal: Xiu then flushed and said: "This is my family's affair—what has it to do with you?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiu snapped, "Family business—none of your affair!"

sentences.zh: 」師垂涕苦諫，秀乃從征。

translations.literal: Shi wept and admonished bitterly; Xiu then followed the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Shi wept and pleaded; Xiu went.

sentences.zh: 秀髮後，州官屬多相連坐，師以此獲免。

translations.literal: After Xiu's hair was removed many prefectural officials were implicated; Shi was spared for this.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiu was punished many officials were implicated; Shi was spared.

sentences.zh: 後加儀同三司。

translations.literal: Later he was made General of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Later Third-rank General.

sentences.zh: 師居職強明，有口辯，而無廉平之稱。

translations.literal: In office Shi was forceful and clear, with a ready tongue, but had no name for integrity and fairness.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was forceful and sharp-tongued but not called fair.

sentences.zh: 卒于刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He died as Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 子恭弟纂，字靈秀，位太府少卿。

translations.literal: Zigong's younger brother Zizuan, styled Lingxiu, held post of Vice Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Zizuan, styled Lingxiu, was Vice Grand Steward.

sentences.zh: 遇害河陰，贈定州刺史。

translations.literal: He was killed at Heyin; posthumously Qinzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Killed at Heyin; posthumously Qinzhou Inspector.

sentences.zh: 子雄。

translations.literal: Son Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Son Xiong.

sentences.zh: 雄字世略，少寬厚，美姿容。

translations.literal: Xiong, styled Shilüe, from youth was generous and of fine appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong, styled Shilüe, was generous and handsome from youth.

sentences.zh: 初仕魏，歷位秘書郎。

translations.literal: He first served Wei and rose to Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Wei as Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 在周以伐齊功，封朔方公，曆冀、平二州刺史，檢校徐州總管。

translations.literal: Under Zhou, for merit in the Qi campaign he was enfeoffed Duke of Shuo and was successively Jizhou and Pingzhou Inspector and Acting Xuzhou Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou, for the Qi campaign he was Duke of Shuo, then Jizhou and Pingzhou Inspector and acting Xuzhou commander.

sentences.zh: 及尉遲迥作亂，時雄家累在相州，迥潛以書誘之。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Jiong rebelled, Xiong's family dependents were at Xiangzhou and Jiong secretly sent a letter to entice him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Jiong rebelled, Xiong's family was at Xiangzhou and Jiong secretly wrote to win him.

sentences.zh: 雄卒不顧。

translations.literal: Xiong in the end paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong ignored it.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝遺書慰勉之。

translations.literal: Sui Wendi sent a letter to comfort and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi sent a letter of comfort.

sentences.zh: 迥遣其將畢義緒據蘭陵，席毗陷昌慮下邑，雄遣眾悉平之。

translations.literal: Jiong sent his general Bi Yixu to hold Lanling; Xi Pi took the lower town of Changyu; Xiong sent troops and pacified all.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong's Bi Yixu held Lanling; Xi Pi took Changyu's lower town; Xiong's troops cleared both.

sentences.zh: 陳人見中原多故，遣其將陳紀、蕭摩訶、任蠻奴、周羅碶、樊毅等侵江北。

translations.literal: The Chen, seeing the central plains in turmoil, sent generals Chen Ji, Xiao Mohe, Ren Mannu, Zhou Luozi, Fan Yi, and others to invade north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Chen sent Chen Ji, Xiao Mohe, Ren Mannu, Zhou Luozi, and Fan Yi north while the plains were in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 自江陵，東距壽陽，人多應之，攻陷城鎮。

translations.literal: From Jiangling east to Shouyang many responded; they attacked and took towns and forts.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiangling to Shouyang many joined them and took towns.

sentences.zh: 雄與吳州總管于顗等擊走之。

translations.literal: Xiong with Wu Regional Commander Yu Yi and others drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong with Yu Yi of Wu and others drove them off.

sentences.zh: 悉復故地。

translations.literal: All former territory was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: All lost ground was recovered.

sentences.zh: 進位上大將軍，拜徐州總管，遷朔州總管。

translations.literal: He advanced to Grand General and was made Xuzhou Regional Commander, then transferred to Shuo Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He became Grand General, Xuzhou commander, then Shuo commander.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，從秦王俊出信州道。

translations.literal: In the pacification of Chen he followed Prince Qin Jun by the Xinzhou route.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying Chen, he followed Prince Qin Jun on the Xinzhou road.

sentences.zh: 陳平，以功進位上柱國，賜子崇爵端氏縣伯，褒為安化縣伯，復鎮朔方。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, for merit he advanced to Pillar of State, enfeoffed son Chong Baron of Duanshi and Bao Baron of Anhua, and again held Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Chen pacified, he was Pillar of State; sons Chong and Bao were barons; he again held Shuo.

sentences.zh: 後歲，上表乞骸骨，征還京師，卒於家。

translations.literal: The next year he memorialized asking to retire; summoned back to the capital, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he asked to retire, was recalled, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 子嵩嗣，大業中，為尚書虞部郎，討北海賊。

translations.literal: Son Song inherited; in the Daye era he was Director of the Parks Bureau and campaigned against the Beihai rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Son Song inherited; in Daye he was Parks Director and fought Beihai rebels.

sentences.zh: 力戰死之，贈正議大夫。

translations.literal: He died fighting hard; posthumously Proper Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in hard fighting; posthumously Proper Counselor.

sentences.zh: 劉尼，代人也。

translations.literal: Liu Ni, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ni, of Dai.

sentences.zh: 曾祖敦，有功于道武，為方面大人。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Dun had merit under Emperor Daowu and was a frontier great chief.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather Dun served Daowu and was a frontier great chief.

sentences.zh: 父婁，為冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Father Lou was Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: Father Lou was Champion General.

sentences.zh: 尼勇果善射，太武見而善之，拜羽林中郎，賜爵昌國子。

translations.literal: Ni was brave, decisive, and skilled at archery; Taiwu saw him and favored him, made him Gentlemen of the Feathered Forest, and enfeoffed him Viscount of Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and skilled at archery, Taiwu favored him, made him Feathered Forest gentleman, and enfeoffed Viscount of Chang.

sentences.zh: 宗愛既殺南安王余於東廟，秘之，唯尼知狀。

translations.literal: When Zong Ai had killed Prince of Nan'an Yu at the eastern temple and kept it secret, only Ni knew the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Ai killed Prince of Nan'an Yu at the eastern temple and hid it, only Ni knew.

sentences.zh: 尼勸愛立文成。

translations.literal: Ni urged Ai to enthrone Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ni urged Ai to enthrone Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 愛自以負罪于景穆，聞而驚曰：「君大癡人！

translations.literal: Ai himself thought he had sinned against Jingmu and, hearing this, said in alarm: "You are a great fool!
translations.idiomatic: Ai, guilty toward Jingmu, cried, "You great fool!

sentences.zh: 皇孫若立，豈忘正平時事乎？

translations.literal: If the imperial grandson is enthroned, will he not remember the Zhengping affair?"
translations.idiomatic: Enthrone the grandson and he will remember Zhengping!"

sentences.zh: 」尼曰：「若爾，立誰？

translations.literal: Ni said: "If so, whom shall we enthrone?"
translations.idiomatic: Ni said, "Then whom do we enthrone?"

sentences.zh: 」愛曰：「待還宮，擢諸王子賢者而立之。

translations.literal: Ai said: "Wait until we return to the palace and choose the worthy among the princes' sons."
translations.idiomatic: Ai said, "Wait till we return and pick a worthy prince's son."

sentences.zh: 」尼懼其有變，密以狀告殿中尚書源賀。

translations.literal: Ni feared he would change course and secretly reported the situation to Palace Attendant Yuan He.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a change, Ni secretly told Palace Attendant Yuan He.

sentences.zh: 時與尼俱典兵宿衛，仍共南部尚書陸麗謀，密奉皇孫。

translations.literal: At the time he and Ni together commanded troops on night guard; they then with Southern Department Director Lu Li plotted and secretly supported the imperial grandson.
translations.idiomatic: He and Ni then held night guard; with Lu Li they secretly backed the grandson.

sentences.zh: 於是，賀與尚書長孫渴侯嚴兵守衛，尼與麗迎文成于苑中。

translations.literal: Thereupon He with Masters of Writing Director Changsun Kehou arrayed troops in strict guard; Ni with Li welcomed Wencheng from the park.
translations.idiomatic: He and Changsun Kehou guarded with troops; Ni and Li brought Wencheng from the park.

sentences.zh: 麗抱文成於馬上，入於京城。

translations.literal: Li held Wencheng in his arms on horseback and entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li carried Wencheng on horseback into the capital.

sentences.zh: 尼馳還東廟，大呼曰：「宗愛殺南安王，大逆不道。

translations.literal: Ni galloped back to the eastern temple and shouted: "Zong Ai killed Prince of Nan'an—great treason!
translations.idiomatic: Ni galloped to the eastern temple and shouted, "Zong Ai killed Prince of Nan'an—treason!

sentences.zh: 皇孫已登大位。

translations.literal: The imperial grandson has already ascended."
translations.idiomatic: The grandson is already enthroned."

sentences.zh: 有詔，宿衛之士，皆可還宮。

translations.literal: There is an edict: all night-guard troops may return to the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Edict: night guard, return to the palace."

sentences.zh: 」眾咸唱萬歲。

translations.literal: The crowd all shouted ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: All shouted long life.

sentences.zh: 賀及渴侯登執宗愛、賈周等，勒兵而入，奉文成于宮門外，入登永安殿。

translations.literal: He and Kehou seized Zong Ai, Jia Zhou, and others, led troops in, and at the palace gate supported Wencheng; he entered and ascended Yong'an Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He and Kehou seized Zong Ai and Jia Zhou, led troops in, and enthroned Wencheng at Yong'an Hall.

sentences.zh: 以尼為內行長，封東安公。

translations.literal: Ni was made Inner Chief and enfeoffed Duke of Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ni was Inner Chief and Duke of Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 尋遷尚書右僕射，為定州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and made Qinzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Vice Director and Qinzhou Inspector.

sentences.zh: 在州清慎，然率多酒醉。

translations.literal: In the province he was pure and cautious, yet often drunk.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was pure but often drunk.

sentences.zh: 文成末，為司徒。

translations.literal: At the end of Wencheng he was Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wencheng he was Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 獻文即位，以尼有大功於先朝，特加尊重，賜別戶四十。

translations.literal: When Xianwen ascended, because Ni had great merit in the former reign he was given special respect and granted forty separate households.
translations.idiomatic: Xianwen gave him special honor and forty separate households for past merit.

sentences.zh: 皇興四年，車駕北征，帝親誓眾，而尼昏醉，兵陳不整。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangxing the imperial carriage campaigned north; the emperor personally swore the host, but Ni was drunk and the battle array was not in order.
translations.idiomatic: Huangxing 4 the emperor campaigned north and swore the troops; Ni was drunk and the ranks were disorderly.

sentences.zh: 帝以其功重，特恕之，免官而已。

translations.literal: The emperor, because his merit was weighty, especially pardoned him and only removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: For his great merit the emperor only dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 延興四年薨，子社生襲。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanxing he died; son She Sheng inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxing 4 he died; son She Sheng inherited.

sentences.zh: 論曰：陸俟以智識見稱，珝乃不替風範，雅杖名節，自立功名；

translations.literal: Discussion: Lu Si was famed for wisdom and discernment; Yu did not fall short of the family style, upheld name and integrity by principle, and built his own fame;
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Lu Si was famed for wisdom; Yu kept the family style, upheld integrity, and made his own name;

sentences.zh: 其傳芳銘典，豈徒然也？

translations.literal: His fragrance in records and canons—was it for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: His fame in records—was it empty?

sentences.zh: 麗忠國奉主，郁為梁棟。

translations.literal: Li was loyal to state and lord, a pillar of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Li served state and lord—a pillar of the realm.

sentences.zh: 資忠履義，赴難如歸，世載克昌，名不虛得。

translations.literal: With loyalty and righteousness he went to hardship as homeward; generations prospered—fame was not empty.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal and righteous, he met hardship like home; the house flourished—fame was earned.

sentences.zh: 睿、琇以沈雅顯達，何末亦披猖？

translations.literal: Rui and Xiu rose through calm elegance—why at the end did they run wild?
translations.idiomatic: Rui and Xiu rose by calm grace—why run wild at the end?

sentences.zh: 子彰令終之美，家聲孔振。

translations.literal: Zizhang's fine end—family renown greatly stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhang's good death shook the family name.

sentences.zh: 仰及彥師俱以孝為本，出處之譽，並可作範人倫。

translations.literal: Yang and Yanshi both took filial piety as root; fame in coming forth and withdrawal both could model human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Yang and Yanshi rooted in filial piety—coming forth or staying back, both could model the world.

sentences.zh: 爽學業有聞，亦人譽也。

translations.literal: Shuang's learning had a name—also men's praise.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang's scholarship was heard—men praised him too.

sentences.zh: 源賀堂堂，非徒武節、觀其翼佐文成，廷抑禪讓，殆乎社稷之臣。

translations.literal: Yuan He was imposing—not only martial bearing; see how he aided Wencheng on the throne, checked abdication in court—nearly a minister of the altars.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan He was imposing—not mere martial show; he raised Wencheng and checked abdication in court—a pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 懷幹略兼舉，出內馳譽，繼跡賢孝，不墮先業。

translations.literal: Huai combined strategy and talent, fame inside and out, followed worthy traces without failing forebears.
translations.idiomatic: Huai joined strategy and talent, won fame at court and border, and did not shame his fathers.

sentences.zh: 子邕功立夏方，身亡冀野。

translations.literal: Ziyong's merit stood in the Xia regions; he died on the Jizhou plain.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong won the Xia frontier and died in Jizhou fields.

sentences.zh: 彪著名齊朝。

translations.literal: Biao was famed in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Biao shone in Qi.

sentences.zh: 師、雄官成隋代，美矣。

translations.literal: Shi and Xiong's offices matured in Sui—beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Shi and Xiong finished their careers in Sui—fine indeed.

sentences.zh: 劉尼忠國，豈徒驍猛之用？

translations.literal: Liu Ni was loyal to the state—was it only for fierce valor?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ni served the state—was it only for fighting?

sentences.zh: 薛提正議忠謀，見害奸閹，痛乎！

translations.literal: Xue Ti's upright counsel and loyal plot met harm from villainous eunuchs—painful!
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ti's loyal counsel died at eunuch hands—how painful!
